# Deploy Hermes on Cloud
Source: https://docs.boxlite.ai/cloud/agent-in-box/hermes

Run the official Hermes image and send tasks through its native Gateway API.

The official Hermes image includes its runtime, tools, and Gateway. Configure Hermes directly, then send a request to its native HTTP API.

Complete the [workstation setup](/cloud/agent-in-box/index#before-you-start). Run all commands below on your workstation.

## Create the box

Use an existing OpenAI Chat Completions-compatible endpoint that supports tool calls. In `create.py`, set `Secret.hosts` to its hostname, without the scheme or path.

Save `create.py`. The prompt reads the real model key on your workstation; only BoxLite's `Secret` configuration receives it.

```python create.py theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
import asyncio
from getpass import getpass
import boxlite

async def main():
    runtime = boxlite.Boxlite.rest(boxlite.BoxliteRestOptions.from_env())
    try:
        box = await runtime.create(
            boxlite.BoxOptions(
                image="docker.io/nousresearch/hermes-agent@sha256:a11574b7fe8e1631d7d88d556677dac693bc058abf558cdeb899155688c1bf05",
                cpus=2, memory_mib=4096, disk_size_gb=10,
                auto_stop=0, auto_delete=0, detach=True,
                cmd=["gateway", "run"],
                network=boxlite.NetworkSpec(inbound=boxlite.InboundNetworkSpec(mode="enabled")),
                env=[("SSL_CERT_FILE", "/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt")],
                secrets=[boxlite.Secret(
                    name="model",
                    value=getpass("Model provider API key: "),
                    hosts=["<YOUR_MODEL_HOST>"],
                )],
            ),
            name="hermes-agent",
        )
        print(box.id)
        await box.start()
    except Exception as exc:
        raise SystemExit(f"{type(exc).__name__}: inspect hermes-agent before retrying creation.") from None
    finally:
        runtime.close()

asyncio.run(main())
```

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
python3 create.py
```

The official image entrypoint and `gateway run` restore Gateway on every boot. This image digest was used for verification.

## Configure Hermes

Save these two files on your workstation. Set `model.base_url` to your endpoint's API base URL and `model.default` to its model ID. These are [Hermes's native model settings](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/configuration).

Keep `<BOXLITE_SECRET:model>` unchanged. `API_SERVER_KEY` is a separate credential for callers of your Gateway.

```yaml config.yaml theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
model:
  provider: custom
  default: <MODEL_ID>
  base_url: https://<YOUR_MODEL_HOST>/v1
  api_mode: chat_completions
  key_env: OPENAI_API_KEY
terminal:
  backend: local
```

```bash .env theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
OPENAI_API_KEY='<BOXLITE_SECRET:model>'
API_SERVER_ENABLED=true
API_SERVER_HOST=0.0.0.0
API_SERVER_PORT=8642
API_SERVER_KEY='<YOUR_RANDOM_GATEWAY_KEY>'
```

Use a separate random key for Gateway callers. You can generate one with `python3 -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))'`.

Keep these files outside Git. Upload them and set ownership for Hermes:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
chmod 600 config.yaml .env
boxlite cp config.yaml hermes-agent:/opt/data/config.yaml
boxlite cp .env hermes-agent:/opt/data/.env
boxlite exec hermes-agent -- sh -c \
  'chown 10000:10000 /opt/data/config.yaml /opt/data/.env && chmod 600 /opt/data/config.yaml /opt/data/.env'
boxlite restart hermes-agent
boxlite network tunnel hermes-agent 8642
```

If `restart` reports `State change in progress`, inspect the box until its state settles. For a `stopped` box, run `boxlite start hermes-agent`; for a `running` box, retry `boxlite restart hermes-agent`. Then register the tunnel if the previous command did not reach that step.

## Send a task

Replace `<YOUR_TUNNEL_URL>` with the returned URL. Run these commands on your workstation, in the directory containing the `.env` file you created above.

The `. ./.env` command loads that file into the current shell so `curl` can use `API_SERVER_KEY`. This key authenticates Gateway callers; the real model-provider key stays in BoxLite Secret. Check readiness first:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
# Load the Gateway caller key from the local .env file.
. ./.env

curl --fail-with-body --max-time 30 '<YOUR_TUNNEL_URL>/health' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_SERVER_KEY"
```

Retry this health request after a few seconds while Gateway starts. Once it succeeds, send the task:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
# Load the Gateway caller key from the local .env file.
. ./.env

curl --fail-with-body --max-time 300 '<YOUR_TUNNEL_URL>/v1/chat/completions' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_SERVER_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"hermes-agent","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Run this exact shell command with your terminal tool: echo HERMES_READY > /opt/data/proof.txt && cat /opt/data/proof.txt"}],"stream":false}'
boxlite exec hermes-agent -- cat /opt/data/proof.txt
# HERMES_READY
```

Wait for Gateway to become ready after the restart. A successful task has `finish_reason: "stop"` and the expected file content.

**Hermes is ready.** Any client supporting its [Gateway API](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/api-server) can submit tasks. No example-specific request client is required.

## Optional: wake on a request

Keep `auto_stop=0` to leave Gateway running. To stop between requests, set `auto_stop=120` in `create.py` and keep [wake on access](/cloud/box-lifecycle#wake-on-access) enabled. Choose an idle interval that fits your workload.

### Restore Gateway when the box starts

The create script preserves the official image entrypoint and saves `gateway run` as its command. The configuration under `/opt/data` and registered port 8642 let the same HTTPS URL reach Gateway after a restart.

Starting Gateway once through `exec` would not save a startup command for subsequent boots. Use the image entrypoint and command from this guide for request-triggered startup.

### Check idle stop and request-triggered wake

![Request-triggered startup and idle stop](https://mintcdn.com/boxliteai/Jyu4ea7vpdHuIh5x/assets/diagrams/cloud-agent-wake.svg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=Jyu4ea7vpdHuIh5x\&q=85\&s=a0e24b5cc0e875209543a808993dd15b)

1. Complete the first task above, which creates `/opt/data/proof.txt`.
2. Stop sending service requests. Use `boxlite inspect hermes-agent` until the state is `stopped`.
3. Send the request below to the same URL, without calling `start`, `exec`, or `cp` first.

On your workstation, run this from the directory containing the same `.env` file. It loads the Gateway caller key, then sends the request that wakes the box:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
# Load the Gateway caller key from the local .env file.
. ./.env

curl --fail-with-body --max-time 300 '<YOUR_TUNNEL_URL>/v1/chat/completions' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_SERVER_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"hermes-agent","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Run this exact shell command with your terminal tool: echo HERMES_AWAKE > /opt/data/awake.txt && cat /opt/data/awake.txt"}],"stream":false}'
```

The request starts the box, its saved command restores Gateway, and Hermes executes the task. After the response, independently verify both files:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
boxlite exec hermes-agent -- cat /opt/data/proof.txt /opt/data/awake.txt
# HERMES_READY
# HERMES_AWAKE
```

The old file checks disk persistence; the new file checks that the awakened agent used its tools. The provider request also exercises the saved Secret substitution after restart. A chat reply alone does not establish either result.

If Cloud returns `503 BOX_STARTING`, wait for its `Retry-After` interval and retry. A timeout has an unknown outcome; inspect the task's result before submitting it again.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Gateway starts as a new process after the box wakes. Do not poll its health endpoint while waiting for idle stop: service traffic can keep the box awake.

For lifecycle controls and background jobs, see [Cloud lifecycle](/cloud/box-lifecycle). Retained disks can still incur [storage charges](/cloud/box-costs).

## When you are finished

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
boxlite stop hermes-agent
# To delete the box and its files:
boxlite rm --force hermes-agent
```


# Manually deploy an agent in a box
Source: https://docs.boxlite.ai/cloud/agent-in-box/index

Create a Cloud box, install your coding agent, and run a real task.

Your agent runs inside a Cloud box, with its own filesystem, shell, and network access. Install it, configure its model connection, and give it a task.

Each guide creates a box with the native SDK, then uses the CLI and the agent's own configuration. Real model-provider keys stay outside the box. **An HTTP service and automatic stop/wake are optional additions.**

## Choose your agent

> [card] [Claude Code](/cloud/agent-in-box/claude-code)
>
> Install the CLI and run a coding task inside the box.

> [card] [Codex](/cloud/agent-in-box/codex)
>
> Run Codex with a Responses-compatible model connection.

> [card] [Pi](/cloud/agent-in-box/pi)
>
> Configure a model provider and use Pi's file and shell tools.

> [card] [OpenCode](/cloud/agent-in-box/opencode)
>
> Bring your provider configuration and run OpenCode in the box.

> [card] [Hermes](/cloud/agent-in-box/hermes)
>
> Use the official image and Hermes Gateway's native HTTP API.

## Before you start

Install the [Cloud CLI and Python SDK](/cloud/quickstart), and configure the native Cloud variables `BOXLITE_REST_URL` and `BOXLITE_API_KEY` on your workstation. Both SDK and CLI use that connection. Keep the Cloud API key outside the box.

Use a model provider supported by your agent. Each guide uses the agent's own authentication and model settings; BoxLite supplies its isolated runtime and credential boundary.

Each `create.py` reads the real provider key on your workstation without echoing it. Pass that value to a host-scoped `Secret`. The agent receives only the matching `<BOXLITE_SECRET:…>` placeholder in its native key setting.

```text theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
Agent inside the box          BoxLite egress proxy          Model provider
Credential placeholder  →  substitute for allowed host  →  authenticated request
```

Match `Secret.hosts` to the model endpoint's hostname. This limits where substitution occurs; use an [egress policy](/cloud/network-policy) to restrict network access separately.

The create scripts configure clients to trust the system CA bundle, including BoxLite's proxy certificate. See [Secret behavior and parameters](/manage-sandbox/secrets-and-security).

`auto_stop=0` keeps the box running, and `auto_delete=0` retains its disk after stopping. Stop it when finished, or choose another [lifecycle policy](/cloud/box-lifecycle). HTTP serving and automatic stop/wake remain optional.

Each agent guide includes its own **Optional: wake on a request** section, with the interface and startup requirements for that agent.

## Add only what you need

| You want to | Continue with |
| - | - |
| Choose when a box stops and wakes | [Cloud lifecycle](/cloud/box-lifecycle) |
| Keep files when replacing the box | [Data across boxes](/cloud/data-across-boxes) |
| Run an agent on your own hardware | [Open-source Agent in a box](/agent-in-box/index) |


# Deploy OpenCode on Cloud
Source: https://docs.boxlite.ai/cloud/agent-in-box/opencode

Install OpenCode, connect a model provider, and run a task inside a Cloud box.

OpenCode runs its tools inside the box. Configure it with its native JSON file and submit a task through `boxlite exec`.

Complete the [workstation setup](/cloud/agent-in-box/index#before-you-start). Run all commands below on your workstation.

## Create the box and install OpenCode

Save `create.py`. Before running it, replace `<YOUR_MODEL_HOST>` with your model endpoint's hostname, without the scheme or path. The prompt reads the real model key on your workstation; only BoxLite's `Secret` configuration receives it.

```python create.py theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
import asyncio
from getpass import getpass
import boxlite

async def main():
    runtime = boxlite.Boxlite.rest(boxlite.BoxliteRestOptions.from_env())
    try:
        box = await runtime.create(
            boxlite.BoxOptions(
                image="node",
                cpus=1, memory_mib=2048, disk_size_gb=10,
                auto_stop=0, auto_delete=0, detach=True,
                env=[("NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS", "/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt")],
                secrets=[boxlite.Secret(
                    name="anthropic",
                    value=getpass("Model provider API key: "),
                    hosts=["<YOUR_MODEL_HOST>"],
                )],
            ),
            name="opencode-agent",
        )
        print(box.id)
        await box.start()
    except Exception as exc:
        raise SystemExit(f"{type(exc).__name__}: inspect opencode-agent before retrying creation.") from None
    finally:
        runtime.close()

asyncio.run(main())
```

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
python3 create.py
```

Install the agent:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
boxlite exec opencode-agent -- \
  npm install -g --prefix /workspace/tools opencode-ai
```

## Configure OpenCode

Save `opencode.json` locally. Keep the `apiKey` placeholder exactly as shown:

```json opencode.json theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
{
  "model": "endpoint/<MODEL_ID>",
  "permission": "allow",
  "provider": {
    "endpoint": {
      "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible",
      "name": "Model endpoint",
      "options": {
        "baseURL": "https://<YOUR_MODEL_HOST>/v1",
        "apiKey": "<BOXLITE_SECRET:anthropic>"
      },
      "models": {
        "<MODEL_ID>": {
          "name": "My model"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Use an OpenAI Chat Completions-compatible endpoint with tool support. Replace the API base URL and `<MODEL_ID>`, and set `Secret.hosts` in `create.py` to the endpoint hostname. For another provider, use [OpenCode's native provider configuration](https://opencode.ai/docs/providers/) and match the Secret's `hosts` to its API endpoint.

`permission: "allow"` lets this trusted task use tools without interactive approval. The agent can use the model connection and access the files and network available inside its box. The real provider key remains outside it.

Upload the placeholder-only configuration:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
chmod 600 opencode.json
boxlite cp opencode.json opencode-agent:/workspace/opencode.json
boxlite exec opencode-agent -- chmod 600 /workspace/opencode.json
```

## Run a task

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
boxlite exec -e OPENCODE_CONFIG=/workspace/opencode.json -w /workspace opencode-agent -- sh -c '
  exec /workspace/tools/bin/opencode run --format json \
  "Run this exact shell command with your terminal tool: echo OPENCODE_READY > /workspace/proof.txt && cat /workspace/proof.txt" < /dev/null
'
boxlite exec opencode-agent -- cat /workspace/proof.txt
# OPENCODE_READY
```

**OpenCode is ready.** Repeat the command with your own task. This example starts a new session for each call.

## Optional: wake on a request

OpenCode provides a [native HTTP server](https://opencode.ai/docs/server/). This walkthrough creates a separate `opencode-http` box and sends tasks through its session API.

Run these commands on your workstation in the directory containing `opencode.json` from above. Automatic stop is optional: use `auto_stop=0` to keep the service running.

### 1. Create the service box

Save `create-http.py`, using the same model Secret and endpoint hostname as above:

```python create-http.py theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
import asyncio
from getpass import getpass
import boxlite

async def main():
    runtime = boxlite.Boxlite.rest(boxlite.BoxliteRestOptions.from_env())
    try:
        box = await runtime.create(
            boxlite.BoxOptions(
                image="node",
                cpus=1, memory_mib=2048, disk_size_gb=10,
                auto_stop=120, auto_resume=True, auto_delete=0, detach=True,
                network=boxlite.NetworkSpec(inbound=boxlite.InboundNetworkSpec(mode="enabled")),
                entrypoint=["/bin/sh", "-c"],
                cmd=["""
until test -x /workspace/tools/bin/opencode && test -s /workspace/opencode.json &&
      test -s /workspace/server-password; do sleep 1; done
export OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD="$(cat /workspace/server-password)"
export OPENCODE_CONFIG=/workspace/opencode.json
cd /workspace
exec /workspace/tools/bin/opencode serve --hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 4096 >> /workspace/http.log 2>&1
"""],
                env=[("NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS", "/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt")],
                secrets=[boxlite.Secret(
                    name="anthropic",
                    value=getpass("Model provider API key: "),
                    hosts=["<YOUR_MODEL_HOST>"],
                )],
            ),
            name="opencode-http",
        )
        print(box.id)
        await box.start()
    except Exception as exc:
        raise SystemExit(f"{type(exc).__name__}: inspect opencode-http before retrying creation.") from None
    finally:
        runtime.close()

asyncio.run(main())
```

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
python3 create-http.py
```

The startup command waits for the installation and configuration, then starts OpenCode on every boot.

### 2. Install and configure the server

Generate a caller password locally. This password protects the HTTP API; it is separate from the model credential.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
python3 - <<'PYTOKEN'
import os
import secrets
from pathlib import Path
os.umask(0o077)
Path("server-password").write_text(secrets.token_hex(32))
PYTOKEN
boxlite exec opencode-http -- npm install -g --prefix /workspace/tools opencode-ai
boxlite cp opencode.json opencode-http:/workspace/opencode.json
boxlite cp server-password opencode-http:/workspace/server-password
boxlite exec opencode-http -- chmod 600 /workspace/server-password
boxlite network tunnel opencode-http 4096
```

Keep `server-password` outside Git. OpenCode reads this caller password inside the box; the real model key stays in BoxLite Secret.

### 3. Create a session and run a task

Set `OPENCODE_URL` to the HTTPS URL from the tunnel command. Keep this shell open for the wake check.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
OPENCODE_URL='<YOUR_TUNNEL_URL>'
curl --fail-with-body --max-time 30 "$OPENCODE_URL/global/health" \
  -u "opencode:$(cat server-password)"
```

Retry the health request after a few seconds if the server is still starting. Create a session and save its ID:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
curl --fail-with-body --max-time 60 "$OPENCODE_URL/session" \
  -u "opencode:$(cat server-password)" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}' > session.json
SESSION_ID=$(python3 -c 'import json; print(json.load(open("session.json"))["id"])')
```

Send a task through the native message API:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
curl --fail-with-body --max-time 240 "$OPENCODE_URL/session/$SESSION_ID/message" \
  -u "opencode:$(cat server-password)" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"parts":[{"type":"text","text":"Run this exact shell command with your terminal tool: echo OPENCODE_HTTP_READY > /workspace/proof.txt && cat /workspace/proof.txt"}]}'
boxlite exec opencode-http -- cat /workspace/proof.txt
# OPENCODE_HTTP_READY
```

Check that the response has no `info.error` and that the independent file check prints the expected value.

### 4. Wait for automatic stop

Stop sending HTTP requests, including health checks. Use only this control-plane check until `Status` is `stopped`:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
boxlite inspect opencode-http
```

Allow two idle minutes. Do not call `start`, `exec`, or `cp` before the next request.

### 5. Wake the server, then submit a task

Use an authenticated health request to wake the box and wait for OpenCode to be ready. This external request starts the box and its saved server command; do not call `start` or `exec` first.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
curl --fail-with-body --max-time 15 --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 2 \
  "$OPENCODE_URL/global/health" \
  -u "opencode:$(cat server-password)"
```

This read-only health check retries startup failures and timeouts. Continue when it succeeds with `"healthy": true`; if it exhausts its retries, inspect the server before submitting a task. Then send a message to the existing session:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
curl --fail-with-body --max-time 240 "$OPENCODE_URL/session/$SESSION_ID/message" \
  -u "opencode:$(cat server-password)" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"parts":[{"type":"text","text":"Run this exact shell command with your terminal tool: echo OPENCODE_HTTP_AWAKE > /workspace/awake.txt && cat /workspace/awake.txt"}]}'
```

The session is retained across the stop. After the task response, verify retained work and the new task:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
boxlite exec opencode-http -- cat /workspace/proof.txt /workspace/awake.txt
# OPENCODE_HTTP_READY
# OPENCODE_HTTP_AWAKE
```

Leave it idle again and it stops automatically. Use the health request for cold startup: direct message submission during startup did not complete in this guide’s Cloud test. A task timeout can leave partial effects; inspect the session before resubmitting it.

### 6. Clean up

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
boxlite rm --force opencode-http
```

## When you are finished

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
boxlite stop opencode-agent
# To delete the box and its files:
boxlite rm --force opencode-agent
```


# Deploy Pi on Cloud
Source: https://docs.boxlite.ai/cloud/agent-in-box/pi

Install Pi, configure its model provider, and run a tool task inside a Cloud box.

Pi reads, writes, and executes commands inside the box. This example uses an OpenAI Chat Completions-compatible endpoint with tool support.

Complete the [workstation setup](/cloud/agent-in-box/index#before-you-start). Run all commands below on your workstation.

## Create the box and install Pi

Save `create.py`. Before running it, replace `<YOUR_MODEL_HOST>` with your model endpoint's hostname, without the scheme or path. The prompt reads the real model key on your workstation; only BoxLite's `Secret` configuration receives it.

```python create.py theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
import asyncio
from getpass import getpass
import boxlite

async def main():
    runtime = boxlite.Boxlite.rest(boxlite.BoxliteRestOptions.from_env())
    try:
        box = await runtime.create(
            boxlite.BoxOptions(
                image="node",
                cpus=1, memory_mib=2048, disk_size_gb=10,
                auto_stop=0, auto_delete=0, detach=True,
                env=[
                    ("NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS", "/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt"),
                    ("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", "<BOXLITE_SECRET:anthropic>"),
                ],
                secrets=[boxlite.Secret(
                    name="anthropic",
                    value=getpass("Model provider API key: "),
                    hosts=["<YOUR_MODEL_HOST>"],
                )],
            ),
            name="pi-agent",
        )
        print(box.id)
        await box.start()
    except Exception as exc:
        raise SystemExit(f"{type(exc).__name__}: inspect pi-agent before retrying creation.") from None
    finally:
        runtime.close()

asyncio.run(main())
```

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
python3 create.py
```

Install the agent:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
boxlite exec pi-agent -- \
  npm install -g --ignore-scripts --prefix /workspace/tools @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent
boxlite exec pi-agent -- mkdir -p /workspace/pi
```

## Connect your model

Use an existing OpenAI Chat Completions-compatible endpoint with tool support. Set `Secret.hosts` in `create.py` to its hostname. Save `models.json`, replacing the API base URL and model ID; set the context and output limits to values supported by your model:

```json models.json theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
{
  "providers": {
    "endpoint": {
      "baseUrl": "https://<YOUR_MODEL_HOST>/v1",
      "api": "openai-completions",
      "apiKey": "<BOXLITE_SECRET:anthropic>",
      "models": [
        {
          "id": "<MODEL_ID>",
          "reasoning": false,
          "input": [
            "text"
          ],
          "contextWindow": 32768,
          "maxTokens": 4096
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Keep the Secret placeholder unchanged. The real provider key stays outside the box. Upload the configuration:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}

```

## Run a task

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
boxlite exec -e PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=/workspace/pi pi-agent -- sh -c '
  exec /workspace/tools/bin/pi --provider endpoint --model "<MODEL_ID>" \
  --mode json --no-session -p \
  "Use your tools to write PI_READY to /workspace/proof.txt, then read it back." < /dev/null
'
boxlite exec pi-agent -- cat /workspace/proof.txt
# PI_READY
```

Check the file and Pi's output. A JSON `stopReason: "error"` means the model request failed, even if the CLI exited with code zero.

**Pi is ready.** Repeat the `exec` command with your own task. `--no-session` makes each call an independent turn.

## Optional: wake on a request

This walkthrough creates a separate `pi-http` box with an authenticated `POST /tasks` endpoint. After two idle minutes, the box stops. Sending another task to the same URL starts the box and runs Pi again.

Run every command below on your workstation, in one directory. You will create two source files and a local caller token. The token's hash goes into the box; the real model key stays in BoxLite's `Secret`.

### 1. Create the HTTP box

Save this as `create-http.py`. Its startup command waits for the files installed in step 3, then starts the service on every boot.

```python create-http.py theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
import asyncio
from getpass import getpass
import boxlite

async def main():
    runtime = boxlite.Boxlite.rest(boxlite.BoxliteRestOptions.from_env())
    try:
        box = await runtime.create(
            boxlite.BoxOptions(
                image="node",
                cpus=1, memory_mib=2048, disk_size_gb=10,
                auto_stop=120, auto_resume=True, auto_delete=0, detach=True,
                network=boxlite.NetworkSpec(inbound=boxlite.InboundNetworkSpec(mode="enabled")),
                entrypoint=["/bin/sh", "-c"],
                cmd=["""
until test -x /workspace/tools/bin/pi && test -s /workspace/pi/models.json &&
      test -s /workspace/server.mjs && test -s /workspace/http-token.sha256; do sleep 1; done
exec node /workspace/server.mjs >> /workspace/http.log 2>&1
"""],
                env=[
                    ("NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS", "/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt"),
                    ("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", "<BOXLITE_SECRET:anthropic>"),
                ],
                secrets=[boxlite.Secret(
                    name="anthropic",
                    value=getpass("Model provider API key: "),
                    hosts=["<YOUR_MODEL_HOST>"],
                )],
            ),
            name="pi-http",
        )
        print(box.id)
        await box.start()
    except Exception as exc:
        raise SystemExit(f"{type(exc).__name__}: inspect pi-http before retrying creation.") from None
    finally:
        runtime.close()

asyncio.run(main())
```

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
python3 create-http.py
```

Use `auto_stop=0` instead if you want this HTTP service to stay running. Keep the value shown to try automatic stop and wake.

Use the same model endpoint and Secret settings as the CLI deployment above.

### 2. Save the HTTP service

Save the complete code below as `server.mjs`. Replace `<MODEL_ID>` with the same model ID from `models.json`. The service accepts `{"prompt":"..."}`, runs one Pi task at a time with a three-minute limit, and returns Pi's JSON result. `POST /tasks` is this example's application API.

> [accordion] server.mjs — complete source
>
> ```javascript server.mjs theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> import http from 'node:http';
> import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
> import { createHash, timingSafeEqual } from 'node:crypto';
> import { execFile } from 'node:child_process';
>
> const tokenHash = Buffer.from(readFileSync('/workspace/http-token.sha256', 'utf8').trim(), 'hex');
> if (tokenHash.length !== 32) throw new Error('Invalid HTTP token hash');
> let busy = false;
>
> function reply(res, status, body) {
>   res.writeHead(status, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
>   res.end(JSON.stringify(body));
> }
>
> const server = http.createServer(async (req, res) => {
>   const authorization = req.headers.authorization ?? '';
>   const token = authorization.slice(7);
>   const suppliedHash = createHash('sha256').update(token).digest();
>   if (!authorization.startsWith('Bearer ') || !timingSafeEqual(suppliedHash, tokenHash)) {
>     return reply(res, 401, { error: 'Unauthorized' });
>   }
>   if (req.method === 'GET' && req.url === '/health') {
>     return reply(res, 200, { ready: true, busy });
>   }
>   if (req.method !== 'POST' || req.url !== '/tasks') {
>     return reply(res, 404, { error: 'Use POST /tasks' });
>   }
>
>   let prompt;
>   try {
>     req.setEncoding('utf8');
>     let body = '';
>     for await (const chunk of req) {
>       body += chunk;
>       if (Buffer.byteLength(body) > 65536) {
>         return reply(res, 413, { error: 'Request too large' });
>       }
>     }
>     ({ prompt } = JSON.parse(body));
>     if (typeof prompt !== 'string' || !prompt.trim()) throw new Error('Invalid prompt');
>   } catch {
>     return reply(res, 400, { error: 'Send JSON with a nonempty prompt string' });
>   }
>   if (busy) return reply(res, 409, { error: 'A task is already running' });
>   busy = true;
>
>   const abort = new AbortController();
>   res.on('close', () => { if (!res.writableEnded) abort.abort(); });
>   const child = execFile('/workspace/tools/bin/pi', [
>     '--provider', 'endpoint', '--model', '<MODEL_ID>', '--mode', 'json', '--no-session', '-p', prompt,
>   ], {
>     env: { ...process.env, PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR: '/workspace/pi' },
>     cwd: '/workspace', detached: true, timeout: 180000, killSignal: 'SIGKILL',
>     maxBuffer: 2 * 1024 * 1024, signal: abort.signal,
>   }, (error, stdout) => {
>     busy = false;
>     if (error && child.pid) {
>       try { process.kill(-child.pid, 'SIGKILL'); } catch {}
>     }
>     if (res.destroyed) return;
>     try {
>       const events = stdout.trim().split('\n').filter(Boolean).map(line => JSON.parse(line));
>       const failed = Boolean(error) || events.some(event => event.message?.stopReason === 'error' || event.message?.stopReason === 'aborted');
>       return reply(res, failed ? 502 : 200, { ok: !failed, events });
>     } catch {
>       return reply(res, error?.killed ? 504 : 502, { error: 'Pi did not return a result' });
>     }
>   });
>   child.stdin.end();
> });
>
> server.requestTimeout = 30000;
> server.listen(8080, '0.0.0.0');
> ```

Only give the caller token to clients allowed to run tasks in this box. Tasks have access to the files and network available to this box.

### 3. Install and start the service

Generate the caller token and its hash locally:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
python3 - <<'PYTOKEN'
import hashlib
import os
import secrets
from pathlib import Path

os.umask(0o077)
token = secrets.token_hex(32)
Path("http-token").write_text(token)
Path("http-token.sha256").write_text(hashlib.sha256(token.encode()).hexdigest())
PYTOKEN
```

Keep `http-token` on your workstation and out of Git. Keep `models.json` from the model setup above. Install Pi, upload the model configuration, service and token hash, then register port 8080:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
boxlite exec pi-http -- \
  npm install -g --ignore-scripts --prefix /workspace/tools @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent
boxlite exec pi-http -- mkdir -p /workspace/pi
boxlite cp models.json pi-http:/workspace/pi/models.json
boxlite cp server.mjs pi-http:/workspace/server.mjs
boxlite cp http-token.sha256 pi-http:/workspace/http-token.sha256
boxlite exec pi-http -- chmod 600 /workspace/http-token.sha256
boxlite network tunnel pi-http 8080
```

The saved startup command starts the service as soon as these files exist. It starts it again after every wake; no attached terminal is required.

### 4. Send the first task

Set `PI_URL` to the HTTPS URL returned by the last command. Keep this shell open for the wake-up check.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
PI_URL='<YOUR_TUNNEL_URL>'
curl --fail-with-body --max-time 30 "$PI_URL/health" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat http-token)"
# {"ready":true,"busy":false}
```

If the service is still starting, retry this health request after a few seconds. Then ask Pi to create a file:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
curl --fail-with-body --max-time 240 "$PI_URL/tasks" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat http-token)" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt":"Run this exact shell command with your terminal tool: echo PI_HTTP_READY > /workspace/proof.txt && cat /workspace/proof.txt"}'
boxlite exec pi-http -- cat /workspace/proof.txt
# PI_HTTP_READY
```

Success means the response contains `"ok": true` and the independent file check prints `PI_HTTP_READY`.

### 5. Wait for automatic stop

Stop sending HTTP requests, including health checks. Run only this control-plane check until `Status` is `stopped`:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
boxlite inspect pi-http
```

Allow two idle minutes. Do not use `start`, `exec`, or `cp` before the next request: the HTTP request should be the action that wakes the box.

### 6. Wake Pi with another task

Send a new task to the same URL:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
curl --fail-with-body --max-time 240 "$PI_URL/tasks" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat http-token)" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt":"Run this exact shell command with your terminal tool: echo PI_HTTP_AWAKE > /workspace/awake.txt && cat /workspace/awake.txt"}'
```

Cloud starts the box; its saved command starts the HTTP service, which runs Pi. After the response, check both files:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
boxlite exec pi-http -- cat /workspace/proof.txt /workspace/awake.txt
# PI_HTTP_READY
# PI_HTTP_AWAKE
```

The first file checks retained work; the second checks that Pi ran tools after wake. Leave the box idle again and it stops automatically.

The file checks verify real tool execution and retained work across a stop and wake.

If Cloud returns `503 BOX_STARTING`, wait for `Retry-After` before retrying. The service returns `401` for a wrong caller token and `409` while another task is running. A timed-out request can have partial effects: inspect its output before resubmitting it.

### 7. Clean up the HTTP box

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
boxlite rm --force pi-http
```

For applications that already use Cloud `exec`, the CLI command above also supports [wake on access](/cloud/box-lifecycle#wake-on-access); this HTTP service is optional.

## When you are finished

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
boxlite stop pi-agent
# To delete the box and its files:
boxlite rm --force pi-agent
```


# API keys and authentication
Source: https://docs.boxlite.ai/cloud/api-keys

Create a BoxLite Cloud API key, hand it to the SDK, CLI, or curl through the environment, and rotate it without downtime.

Every call to BoxLite Cloud carries one credential: an API key you create in the console and send as a bearer token. There is no local runtime to fall back on and no permissive mode — a request without a valid key does not create a box.

## What a key grants

A key is a **fleet-level credential, not a read-only token**. Its holder can create,
start, inspect, and remove boxes on your account, manage your image catalog, and spend
your account's capacity. There is no narrower key to issue instead — the create dialog
offers no permission choice.

| Property | Value |
| - | - |
| Format | `blk_live_...` |
| Transport | `Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>` |
| Permissions | `Full` on keys issued today. Older keys may show `Boxes`, which cannot reach the image endpoints — those answer `403` |
| Expiry | Set when you create the key; the default is `No expiration` |

> [!NOTE]
>
> The create dialog describes the key as *"Boxes API access — this key can create and
> manage Boxes. Shared Linux base images are available automatically."* Read that as a
> floor, not a ceiling: the key the dialog issues lands in the list with **`Full`** in its
> **PERMISSIONS** column. Check that column rather than the dialog when you need to know
> what a key can reach.

## Create a key in the console

Sign in to the console at `https://app.boxlite.ai`, open **API Keys**, and click **Create Key**. The dialog asks for two things:

| Field | Required | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| **Key Name** | Yes | How you will recognize the key in the list — use the environment or service that will hold it, such as `ci-pull-requests`. |
| **Expires** | No | An optional expiration date. Defaults to `No expiration`. |

The full key is shown once, at creation. **Copy it before you close the dialog** — from then on the list view shows only a masked form such as `blk_live_********************UHK`.

The list view gives you one row per key with these columns:

| Column | What it tells you |
| - | - |
| **NAME** | The name you chose. |
| **KEY** | The masked key, enough to match a key against a value you hold. |
| **PERMISSIONS** | The API surface the key can reach. `Full` reaches everything, including images; `Boxes` cannot reach the image endpoints. This is the authoritative value — the create dialog does not show it. |
| **CREATED** | When the key was issued. |
| **LAST USED** | The signal to check before you delete a key: a key with no recent use is safe to remove. |
| **EXPIRES** | The expiration date, or nothing when the key does not expire. |

## Give the key to your code

BoxLite Cloud reads two environment variables. Both the SDKs and the CLI use the same names, so one export pair serves all of them:

| Variable | Required | Value |
| - | - | - |
| `BOXLITE_API_KEY` | Yes | Your `blk_live_...` key. |
| `BOXLITE_REST_URL` | Yes | `https://api.boxlite.ai` |

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
read -rs BOXLITE_API_KEY   # prompts without echoing; nothing lands in shell history
export BOXLITE_API_KEY
export BOXLITE_REST_URL="https://api.boxlite.ai"
```

Read the key from the environment at runtime and pass it as an `ApiKeyCredential`. The snippets below construct a client and list your boxes, which is the cheapest way to prove a credential works.

> [tab] Python
>
> ```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> # check_credentials.py — prove the key in your environment reaches Cloud
> # Run: python check_credentials.py
> import asyncio
> import os
>
> from boxlite import ApiKeyCredential, Boxlite, BoxliteRestOptions
>
> api_key = os.environ.get("BOXLITE_API_KEY")
> if not api_key:
>     raise SystemExit("Set BOXLITE_API_KEY to your blk_live_... key before running this.")
>
>
> async def main() -> None:
>     rt = Boxlite.rest(
>         BoxliteRestOptions(
>             url=os.environ.get("BOXLITE_REST_URL", "https://api.boxlite.ai"),
>             credential=ApiKeyCredential(api_key),
>         )
>     )
>
>     try:
>         boxes = await rt.list_info()
>         print(f"Credential accepted. Boxes visible to this key: {len(boxes)}")
>         for info in boxes:
>             print(f"  - {info.id} name={info.name} status={info.state.status}")
>     except Exception as exc:
>         # A rejected key surfaces here as an HTTP 401
>         print(f"Credential check failed: {exc!r}")
>
>
> if __name__ == "__main__":
>     asyncio.run(main())
> ```

> [tab] Node
>
> ```typescript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> // check-credentials.ts — prove the key in your environment reaches Cloud
> // Run: npx tsx check-credentials.ts
> import { JsBoxlite, BoxliteRestOptions, ApiKeyCredential } from "@boxlite-ai/boxlite";
>
> async function main(): Promise<void> {
>   const apiKey = process.env.BOXLITE_API_KEY;
>   if (!apiKey) {
>     throw new Error("Set BOXLITE_API_KEY to your blk_live_... key before running this.");
>   }
>
>   // The runtime class is JsBoxlite; there is no bare Boxlite export
>   const rt = JsBoxlite.rest(
>     new BoxliteRestOptions({
>       url: process.env.BOXLITE_REST_URL ?? "https://api.boxlite.ai",
>       credential: new ApiKeyCredential(apiKey),
>     }),
>   );
>
>   try {
>     const boxes = await rt.listInfo();
>     console.log(`Credential accepted. Boxes visible to this key: ${boxes.length}`);
>     for (const info of boxes) {
>       console.log(`  - ${info.id} name=${info.name} status=${info.state.status}`);
>     }
>   } catch (err) {
>     // A rejected key surfaces here as an HTTP 401
>     console.error("Credential check failed:", err instanceof Error ? err.message : err);
>   } finally {
>     rt.close(); // synchronous
>   }
> }
>
> main();
> ```

### Load the whole configuration from the environment

`BoxliteRestOptions.from_env()` builds the options object for you, wrapping `BOXLITE_API_KEY` into an `ApiKeyCredential` automatically. It is the shortest correct form for CI jobs and services, where the credential is injected by the platform rather than typed by a person.

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
# from_env_check.py — let the SDK read BOXLITE_REST_URL and BOXLITE_API_KEY for you
import asyncio

from boxlite import Boxlite, BoxliteRestOptions


async def main() -> None:
    try:
        opts = BoxliteRestOptions.from_env()
    except Exception as exc:
        # Raised when BOXLITE_REST_URL is unset
        print(f"Missing configuration: {exc!r}")
        print("Set BOXLITE_REST_URL and BOXLITE_API_KEY, then run this again.")
        return

    rt = Boxlite.rest(opts)
    try:
        boxes = await rt.list_info()
        print(f"Credential accepted. Boxes visible to this key: {len(boxes)}")
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"Credential check failed: {exc!r}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

For the full list of variables `from_env()` reads, see [Manage remote sandboxes over REST](/guides/agent-service-endpoint). One of them, `BOXLITE_REST_PATH_PREFIX`, exists for self-hosted control planes — leave it unset for Cloud, and see the `path_prefix` row under [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) below.

## Persist credentials for the CLI

Exports live and die with a shell. `boxlite auth login` writes the credential to a profile in `~/.boxlite/credentials.toml` instead, so every later `boxlite` command in every shell finds it.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
# Read the key without echoing it, then hand it to the CLI over stdin so it
# never appears in argv or in your shell history
read -rs BOXLITE_API_KEY
printf '%s' "$BOXLITE_API_KEY" | boxlite auth login \
  --url https://api.boxlite.ai --api-key-stdin

boxlite auth status    # what is stored locally, no network call
boxlite auth whoami    # confirm the identity the service sees, via GET /v1/me
boxlite auth logout    # delete the stored credential
```

Profiles let one machine hold several identities. Each profile stores its own URL, bearer, and route prefix; `--profile <NAME>` or `BOXLITE_PROFILE` selects one, and the default profile is named `default`.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
# Store a second identity, then use it for one command
printf '%s' "$STAGING_KEY" | boxlite auth login --profile staging \
  --url https://api.boxlite.ai --api-key-stdin
boxlite --profile staging ps
```

One interaction is worth knowing before it surprises you: `BOXLITE_API_KEY` in the environment overrides **only** the bearer from the stored profile, not the profile's URL or route prefix. A stale export can therefore send the wrong key to the right service. For the complete flag table, see [`boxlite auth`](/reference/cli#boxlite-auth).

## Handle keys safely

* **Never commit a key, and never put it in argv.** Both source control and shell history are searchable forever. Read the key with `read -rs` and pass it through the environment or over stdin, as the snippets above do.
* **Use one key per environment.** Separate keys for local development, CI, and production mean the **LAST USED** column tells you something, and a leak from CI does not force you to re-credential your laptop.
* **Set an expiry when the key has a known lifetime.** A key issued for a two-week migration should stop working in two weeks, not in two years.
* **Rotate by creating first, deleting second.** Create the replacement key, deploy it everywhere the old key was used, confirm traffic on the new key, and only then delete the old one. Deleting first means every box the old key manages goes unreachable until the new key lands.
* **Give agents the narrowest key you can.** A key holder can create and remove boxes on your account, so an agent that only needs one box still gets a key that could remove them all — keep that key on your infrastructure and out of any prompt or model context.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| - | - | - |
| `401 Unauthorized` on every call | The key is missing from the request, mistyped, or was deleted in the console. | Confirm the value starts with `blk_live_` and that its masked form matches a live row in **API Keys**. Cloud has no permissive mode, so there is no configuration that makes an unauthenticated request succeed. |
| `SystemExit: Set BOXLITE_API_KEY ...`, or the CLI runs against your local runtime | The process did not inherit the export — a new shell, a cron job, or a service manager with its own environment. | Export both variables in the process that actually runs, or store the credential with `boxlite auth login` so it does not depend on the shell. |
| An HTML page comes back instead of a box payload, with a `200` status | The base URL points at the console host `https://app.boxlite.ai`. The console serves the dashboard page on paths it does not recognise, so a wrong base URL does not fail loudly — it returns markup your client cannot parse. | Set `BOXLITE_REST_URL` to exactly `https://api.boxlite.ai`. That is the API host; `app.boxlite.ai` is the console you sign in to. |
| Calls that worked before start returning `401` | The key passed the date in its **EXPIRES** column. | Create a replacement key, update the environment, then delete the expired row. |
| `RuntimeError('box not found: {"detail":"Not Found"}')` while the key is valid | A `path_prefix` is being sent. Cloud serves `/v1/boxes` directly; the route prefix belongs to the open-source reference server, which mounts routes under `/v1/{prefix}/boxes`. | Drop `path_prefix` from `BoxliteRestOptions`, unset `BOXLITE_REST_PATH_PREFIX`, and drop `--path-prefix` from CLI invocations. See [BoxLite Cloud vs open source](/cloud/vs-opensource). |
| `boxlite auth whoami` fails while `boxlite auth status` looks correct | `status` reads local state only; `whoami` calls `GET /v1/me`. A stored credential can be well-formed and still be rejected. | Log in again with the current key, and check whether a stale `BOXLITE_API_KEY` export is overriding the profile's bearer. |

# Managing billing
Source: https://docs.boxlite.ai/cloud/billing

Fund your wallet, set automatic reload so boxes never stop for lack of balance, read what you have actually been charged, and know the per-box ceilings that apply to every box in your organization.

This page covers running the account. For what a box costs see [What a box costs](/cloud/box-costs); for whether to subscribe see [Wallet or a plan?](/cloud/plans).

Your **wallet** is a prepaid balance. It funds usage once a plan's included quota is consumed, and it funds everything if you have no plan.

## The wallet

The **Wallet** tab shows your available balance and what you have spent this month.

> [!NOTE]
>
> The figure shown as **available** is your *ongoing* balance: it already reflects usage accrued this cycle but not yet settled. That is why it drifts downward while boxes run, with no payment having been taken.

### Add funds

Click **Top up** and pick a preset amount — **$25**, **$500**, **$1,000**, or **$2,000** — or enter a custom amount. The console redirects you to Stripe to complete the payment.

### Set automatic reload

Manual top-ups are why wallets hit zero at 3am. Automatic reload watches the balance and refills it: set a **threshold** to drop below and a **target** to be refilled to, and the console reads the result back as `Below $20.00 → $100.00`.

It prefills $20 and $100. Reload stays off until you save it, and it charges your connected card — so attach one first.

### Connect a payment method

Until a card is attached the console shows the payment method as not connected, with a **Connect** button beside it. Connecting one earns an additional **\$100 of credits**.

### Redeem a coupon

**Redeem coupon** takes a coupon code and credits the account. Credits are tracked separately from your topped-up balance, so the console shows credits remaining against credits granted.

## Read the usage chart

The **Usage** tab answers "where is my money going" with settled cost by day for the last 30 days, as either a chart or a list. It splits cost into two series:

| Series | What it represents |
| - | - |
| **Quota-covered** | Cost your plan's included quota absorbed |
| **From wallet** | Cost your prepaid wallet balance paid for |

The moment worth watching is when the second series starts growing: that is where this cycle's quota ran out and your boxes began drawing on money you topped up.

This tab is the authority on what you were actually charged — the hourly figures in the **New Box** dialog and on [What a box costs](/cloud/box-costs) are estimates. **Check it before you scale a workload up:** see what a typical day already costs, then multiply by the fan-out you are about to add.

## Per-box resource ceilings

**Billing** also publishes the ceilings that apply to every box in your organization:

| Resource | Ceiling per box |
| - | - |
| Compute | 4 vCPU |
| Memory | 32 GiB |
| Storage | 120 GiB |

These bound how large a **single box** can be — a different constraint from your plan's concurrency limit, which bounds how many boxes run at once. A request above a ceiling is rejected before the box is created, so you get a clear error rather than a box that fails later. See [Choose a size](/cloud/box-sizes) for the presets and custom fields available within them.

If a workload genuinely needs a larger single box, that is an Enterprise conversation — custom limits go through [sales@boxlite.ai](mailto:sales@boxlite.ai).

## Troubleshooting

| Situation | Why it happens | What to do |
| - | - | - |
| Wallet balance has reached zero and your quota is consumed | There is nothing left to fund usage this cycle | Top up on the **Wallet** tab, or redeem a coupon code |
| Boxes stopped and the console reports credits depleted | Nothing remains to fund them, so the platform stops boxes rather than running up an unfunded bill | Top up, then set automatic reload so it does not recur |
| Automatic reload is configured but never fires | Reload needs a card to charge, and no payment method is connected | Connect a card on the **Wallet** tab |
| The available balance drops while you have taken no payment | The figure is the ongoing balance, which already includes usage accrued but not yet settled | Nothing is wrong. Compare against the **Usage** tab for settled cost |
| The payment method shows as not connected | No card is attached to the account | Click **Connect** on the **Wallet** tab. Connecting one also earns \$100 of credits |
| A box request asks for more CPU, memory, or disk than allowed | It exceeds a per-box ceiling for the organization | Lower the request, or spread the work across several boxes within your concurrency limit |
| Cost is higher than expected with no obvious cause | Stopped boxes are still billed for their disk until they are deleted | Delete boxes you have finished with. See [What each box state costs](/cloud/box-costs#what-each-box-state-costs) |

## Next steps

> [card] [What a box costs](/cloud/box-costs)
>
> Rates, worked examples, and the two controls that cap what you keep paying.

> [card] [Wallet or a plan?](/cloud/plans)
>
> The usage level at which a subscription starts costing less.


# What a box costs
Source: https://docs.boxlite.ai/cloud/box-costs

The three metered rates, the formula they combine into, what the standard sizes come to per hour and per month, and exactly which hours are counted.

A box rents three things by the hour: vCPU, memory, and disk. This page turns those rates into the numbers you can plan against.

## Rates

| Resource | Unit | Rate |
| - | - | - |
| vCPU | per vCPU-hour | **\$0.0504** |
| Memory | per GiB-hour | **\$0.0144** |
| Disk | per GiB-hour | **\$0.00018** |

A box's hourly price is the plain sum, with no tiers and no rounding:

```
hourly = vCPU × $0.0504  +  memory_GiB × $0.0144  +  disk_GiB × $0.00018
```

Nothing else is metered. There is no charge for network traffic, API requests, mounted volumes, preview URLs, or the time a box spends booting.

## What the standard sizes cost

The three sizes in the **New Box** dialog, plus the largest box your organization can request:

| Size | vCPU / memory / disk | Per hour | 30 days running | 30 days stopped |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| **Small** | 1 / 1 GiB / 10 GiB | \$0.0666 | \$47.95 | \$1.30 |
| **Medium** | 2 / 4 GiB / 20 GiB | \$0.1620 | \$116.64 | \$2.59 |
| **Large** | 4 / 8 GiB / 50 GiB | \$0.3258 | \$234.58 | \$6.48 |
| Organization ceiling | 4 / 32 GiB / 120 GiB | \$0.6840 | \$492.48 | \$15.55 |

Two readings of that table matter.

**Per invocation, boxes are almost free.** A 30-second code-interpreter run on a Small box costs $0.00056 — ten thousand of them come to $5.55. Per-run cost is not where Cloud bills get large.

**Per month left running, they are not.** The gap between the last two columns is the whole cost story, and the next section is why it exists. [Cost controls](/cloud/cost-controls) is how you close it.

To make a box cheaper, cut vCPU first: one vCPU-hour costs as much as **3.5 GiB-hours of memory** or **280 GiB-hours of disk**. Trimming disk is not worth the thought — it is 2–3% of a running box.

## What each box state costs

| Box state | vCPU | Memory | Disk |
| - | - | - | - |
| **Running** | charged | charged | charged |
| **Stopped** | — | — | **charged** |
| Creating or starting | — | — | — |
| **Deleted** | — | — | — |

A stopped box has given back its compute but still occupies its disk, and it is billed for that disk until the box is deleted.

One forgotten box is loose change. A hundred of them is $130–$650 a month for nothing, and nothing clears them for you.

### How the hours are counted

Compute and disk are charged over different intervals. The two clocks start together and stop at different moments:

| Moment | vCPU + memory | Disk |
| - | - | - |
| Box created but never started | not charged | not charged |
| Box reaches **running** | clock starts | clock starts |
| You **request a stop** | **clock stops** | keeps running |
| Box is stopped, however long | not charged | keeps running |
| You **request deletion** | not charged | **clock stops** |

Two of those moments are earlier than you might expect, and both are in your favor:

* **Compute stops billing when the stop is requested**, not when the box has finished shutting down. You do not pay vCPU or memory for the shutdown itself.
* **Disk stops billing when deletion is requested**, not when teardown completes.

There is **no minimum billable duration and no rounding up to a whole hour**. The platform records the exact moment of each transition, so a box that runs for four minutes is charged for four minutes at the hourly rate. A box you create and never start costs nothing at all.

## Estimates and settlement

The **New Box** dialog quotes what your chosen size costs to run for one hour. Treat it as an estimate — your actual charge is settled from recorded usage, and the **Usage** tab is the authority on what you were charged. See [Managing billing](/cloud/billing#read-the-usage-chart).

## Troubleshooting

| Situation | Why it happens | What to do |
| - | - | - |
| A box you stopped days ago is still adding to your bill | A stopped box keeps its disk and is charged for it until deleted | Delete it, or set `auto_delete` so it clears itself. See [Cost controls](/cloud/cost-controls) |
| Cost is far higher than the size suggests | Something keeps the box busy, so it never goes idle and `auto_stop` never fires. A busy box is not an idle box | Check what is running inside it, or stop the box explicitly when the work finishes |
| Creation fails with `auto_delete must be greater than auto_stop` | Both are non-zero but `auto_delete` is not larger | Raise `auto_delete` above `auto_stop`, or set `auto_delete=0` to disable deletion |
| A request for more than 4 vCPU, 32 GiB of memory, or 120 GiB of disk is rejected | Those are per-box ceilings for the whole organization, enforced before the box is created | Lower the request or split the work across boxes. See [Per-box resource ceilings](/cloud/billing#per-box-resource-ceilings) |

## Next steps

> [card] [Cost controls](/cloud/cost-controls)
>
> The two lifecycle controls that stop a finished box from charging you.

> [card] [Wallet or a plan?](/cloud/plans)
>
> The usage level at which a subscription starts costing less.


# Create, reuse, and remove a box from code
Source: https://docs.boxlite.ai/cloud/box-from-code

The full create-start-use-remove cycle over REST, reusing a box by name, managing one from the console, and passing environment variables.

One runnable script for the whole cycle, plus the two things people get wrong: reusing a box by name, and tearing it down when an exception fires.

## Prerequisites

* An API key from the console, exported as `BOXLITE_API_KEY`. See [API keys](/cloud/api-keys).
* `pip install boxlite`, and the REST URL exported as `BOXLITE_REST_URL`. See [Quickstart](/cloud/quickstart).

## Create, reuse, and remove a box from code

Name your box. The name is how a second process — a worker, a retry, tomorrow's cron job — finds the same box instead of building a new one.

`name` is a parameter of `rt.create(...)`, not a field of `BoxOptions`. Passing `name=` inside `BoxOptions` fails at construction.

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
import asyncio
import os

from boxlite import ApiKeyCredential, Boxlite, BoxliteRestOptions, BoxOptions

BOX_NAME = "nightly-report-runner"

async def main() -> None:
    box_id = None
    rt = None
    try:
        # export BOXLITE_API_KEY=<YOUR_API_KEY> before running
        rt = Boxlite.rest(BoxliteRestOptions(
            url=os.environ.get("BOXLITE_REST_URL", "https://api.boxlite.ai"),
            credential=ApiKeyCredential(os.environ["BOXLITE_API_KEY"]),
        ))

        box = await rt.create(
            BoxOptions(image="ghcr.io/boxlite-ai/boxlite-agent-base:v0.1.0"),
            name=BOX_NAME,
        )
        box_id = box.id
        await box.start()

        # REST boxes take command arguments as a list
        execution = await box.exec("sh", args=["-c", "echo report ready"])
        output = ""
        async for line in execution.stdout():
            output += line
        result = await execution.wait()
        print(f"exit code: {result.exit_code}")
        print(output)

        # any process holding your API key can pick the same box up by name
        again = await rt.get(BOX_NAME)
        if again is None:
            raise RuntimeError(f"box {BOX_NAME} not found")
        print(f"reused box: {again.id}")
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"cloud box failed: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
    finally:
        # remove is called on the runtime, so this script can be run again with the same name
        if rt is not None and box_id:
            try:
                await rt.remove(box_id, force=True)
            except Exception as exc:
                print(f"remove failed: {exc}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

Three shapes to keep in mind on Cloud:

* `Boxlite.rest(...)` is constructed synchronously; `create`, `start`, `exec`, and `remove` are all awaited.
* `box.exec("echo", args=["hi"])` takes its arguments as a list.
* Teardown is `await rt.remove(box.id, force=True)` on the runtime.

`rt.get_or_create(...)` creates a box or reuses an existing one with the same name in a single call. For the state model behind create, start, stop, and remove — and for the signatures of the runtime methods — see [Lifecycle](/manage-sandbox/lifecycle).

## Manage a box from the console

The **Boxes** list is the management surface for a box, so you do not need your own tooling to see what you are running. Each row shows the box name, its id, and its status, and carries two actions:

| Action | What it does |
| - | - |
| **Stop** | Stops a running box, keeping its disk |
| **More** → **Delete** | Removes the box, after a confirmation that warns the action cannot be undone |

BoxLite generates a name for a box you create in the console — a two-word pair such as `golden-lynx` — and a short mixed-case id such as `9z8vat0excp9`. When you create a box from code you pass your own name, which is what makes a box findable later.

Use the list to catch boxes a crashed script left behind. Filter by name, check which are still `RUNNING`, and stop or delete them.

## Environment variables and secrets

`BoxOptions` accepts `env` for plain configuration and `secrets` for values that should not sit in your box's environment or logs. Their shapes differ between Python and Node, and secrets carry extra options such as host scoping, so use the pages that own those tables: [Environment and startup](/manage-sandbox/environment) and [Inject secrets and harden a box](/manage-sandbox/secrets-and-security).

Keep your BoxLite API key out of both. It belongs in the environment of the process that calls `Boxlite.rest(...)`, not inside the box.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| - | - | - |
| `BoxOptions(name="my-box")` fails with a no-such-field error | `name` belongs to the create call | Use `await rt.create(BoxOptions(...), name="my-box")` |
| `box.exec("sh", "-c", "echo hi")` fails on Cloud | REST boxes take arguments as a list | Use `box.exec("sh", args=["-c", "echo hi"])` |
| `await box.remove()` raises an attribute error | Removal happens on the runtime | Use `await rt.remove(box.id, force=True)` |
| A box is still billing after your script crashed | The script died before its cleanup ran | Open the **Boxes** list and stop or delete the leftovers, or list them from code with `await rt.list_info()` and remove each with `await rt.remove(box_id, force=True)`. Setting **Delete after stopping** on future boxes lets the platform reclaim them for you |

## Next steps

> [card] [Boxes](/cloud/boxes)
>
> Everything else about configuring a box on Cloud.


# Box lifecycle on Cloud
Source: https://docs.boxlite.ai/cloud/box-lifecycle

The three controls that decide when a Cloud box stops, whether it wakes again, and when it is deleted — and the idle rule that can end a job you thought was safe.

A Cloud box does not run until you stop it. The platform stops it when it looks idle, wakes it when you reach for it, and can delete it once it has been stopped for a while. These three controls are the most consequential settings on a box.

## Prerequisites

* An API key from the console, exported as `BOXLITE_API_KEY`. See [API keys](/cloud/api-keys).
* `pip install boxlite`, and the REST URL exported as `BOXLITE_REST_URL`. See [Quickstart](/cloud/quickstart).

## Lifecycle on Cloud

Three controls in the **New Box** dialog govern how long your box lives. They behave differently from a box you run yourself, and the first one can end a job you thought was safe.

| Control | Choices | Default |
| - | - | - |
| **Stop when idle** | `Never`, `5 min`, `15 min`, `30 min`, `1 hour`, `4 hours`, or a custom value | `15 min` |
| **Wake on access** | A switch | On |
| **Delete after stopping** | A delay, or `Never` to keep the box | `Never` |

Set them in the console when you create a box there, or from code with three `BoxOptions` fields:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| - | - | - |
| `auto_stop` | `int` (seconds) | Idle time before the box is stopped. `0` disables it |
| `auto_delete` | `int` (seconds) | Time spent stopped before the box is deleted. `0` disables it |
| `auto_resume` | `bool` | Whether an incoming operation resumes the box after an auto-stop |

Two rules to know before you set them:

* **`auto_delete` must be greater than `auto_stop`** when both are non-zero. Otherwise creation fails with `auto_delete must be greater than auto_stop`, because a box that deletes itself before it stops has no reachable state.
* **The defaults come from the platform, not from the SDK.** Omit these fields and the SDK leaves them out of the request entirely, so the platform applies its own defaults: `auto_stop=900` (15 idle minutes), `auto_delete=0` (never), and `auto_resume=true`. A box created from code therefore behaves like one created in the console — **it will stop itself after 15 idle minutes whether you asked for that or not.**

The console's `15 min` corresponds to `auto_stop=900`, which is the same value a box created from code receives by default. To keep a box running through unattended work, you must pass `auto_stop` explicitly — see [Stop when idle](#stop-when-idle).

The field names matter: `idle_timeout`, `stop_when_idle`, `wake_on_access`, `delete_after_stopping`, and `auto_pause` are not fields of `BoxOptions` and each fails construction with a no-such-field error.

## Stop when idle

Idleness is measured at the boundary of the box, not inside it. The console is explicit:

> Idle means no SDK, terminal or preview traffic. Work running inside the box does not count — a long job can be stopped mid-run.

That is the single most important sentence on this page. A 40-minute build that you kick off and then stop talking to looks idle from the outside, and the platform stops it at 15 minutes with the build half-finished.

Two ways to keep a long job alive:

* **Keep touching the box from your client.** Poll the job while it runs — read its progress file or check its process — so real SDK traffic keeps arriving.
* **Raise the idle timeout, or disable it.** In the console, pick a longer value or `Never`; from code, pass a larger `auto_stop` or `auto_stop=0`. Disabling it is the right choice for a box whose whole purpose is unattended work — and the one that makes you responsible for tearing it down.

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
import asyncio

async def run_long_job(box) -> int:
    """Start a long job, then poll it so the box keeps seeing SDK traffic."""
    starter = await box.exec("sh", args=["-c", "nohup ./build.sh > /tmp/build.log 2>&1 & echo started"])
    await starter.wait()

    while True:
        # each exec is SDK traffic, so the box does not look idle
        probe = await box.exec("sh", args=["-c", "pgrep -f build.sh > /dev/null && echo running || echo done"])
        state = ""
        async for line in probe.stdout():
            state += line
        await probe.wait()

        if "done" in state:
            break
        await asyncio.sleep(60)

    tail = await box.exec("tail", args=["-n", "20", "/tmp/build.log"])
    async for line in tail.stdout():
        print(line, end="")
    result = await tail.wait()
    return result.exit_code
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> Pass this helper a box you already created and started, using the pattern in [Create, reuse, and remove a box from code](/cloud/box-from-code). Choose a poll interval comfortably shorter than the box's idle timeout.

## Wake on access

Resume is on by default — the console switch starts on, and `auto_resume` defaults to `true` over the API. With it enabled, a stopped box comes back on its own when you reach for it:

SDK exec, file operations, and terminal attach can wake a stopped box. Requests to a registered HTTPS service URL can also start the box and reach its saved startup service. See the [Hermes Gateway walkthrough](/cloud/agent-in-box/hermes#optional-wake-on-a-request).

Waking a stopped box starts new guest processes with the retained disk. It does not restore process memory; a service must have a saved startup command.

This is what makes a named Cloud box feel durable: your script calls `exec` after a weekend, the box restarts with its disk intact, and your code carries on. Enable it for any box you intend to reuse. Leave it off when a stop should be final until you intervene.

## Delete after stopping

**Delete after stopping** defaults to `Never`, so a stopped box keeps its disk and stays addressable by name. Set a delay when you want the platform to reclaim throwaway boxes for you instead of remembering to call `remove` yourself.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| - | - | - |
| A long job dies partway through, around the 15-minute mark | **Stop when idle** counts only SDK, terminal, and preview traffic. Work inside the box does not count, so the platform stopped the box mid-run | Poll the box from your client while the job runs, or raise or disable the idle timeout for that box in the console |
| `exec` against a stopped box fails instead of restarting it | Resume was switched off for that box. It is on by default in both the console and over the API, so this only happens if it was turned off at creation | Recreate the box with **Wake on access** left on, or `auto_resume=True` from code — that is what lets SDK exec, file operations, and terminal attach bring a stopped box back |
| `BoxOptions(idle_timeout=3600)` or `BoxOptions(auto_pause=True)` fails with a no-such-field error | Those are not the field names | Use `auto_stop`, `auto_delete`, and `auto_resume` — see [Lifecycle on Cloud](/cloud/box-lifecycle) |
| Creation fails with `auto_delete must be greater than auto_stop` | `auto_delete` is non-zero but not larger than `auto_stop` | Raise `auto_delete` above `auto_stop`, or set `auto_delete=0` to disable deletion |
| A box created from code stopped in the middle of unattended work | Omitting `auto_stop` does not disable it — the platform applies its `900` second default, and work inside the box does not count as activity | Pass `auto_stop=0` to disable auto-stop, or a value longer than the job. See [Stop when idle](#stop-when-idle) |
| A box you expected to keep running was gone or stopped after 15 minutes | Same cause: `auto_stop` defaults to `900`, not to `0` | Set `auto_stop` explicitly for any box doing unattended work |
| A box you expected to reuse is gone | Its **Delete after stopping** delay elapsed after an idle stop | Create the replacement with **Delete after stopping** set to `Never`, and put anything you must keep on a volume — see [Volumes on Cloud](/cloud/volumes) |

## Next steps

> [card] [Boxes](/cloud/boxes)
>
> Everything else about configuring a box on Cloud.


# Choose a size for a Cloud box
Source: https://docs.boxlite.ai/cloud/box-sizes

The three preset sizes, the per-organization ceilings that bound any single box, and the SDK fields that set them.

Size is vCPU, memory, and disk. Pick the smallest preset that runs your workload comfortably — it is what you pay for by the hour.

## Prerequisites

* An API key from the console, exported as `BOXLITE_API_KEY`. See [API keys](/cloud/api-keys).
* `pip install boxlite`, and the REST URL exported as `BOXLITE_REST_URL`. See [Quickstart](/cloud/quickstart).

## Choose a size

The console offers three presets and a custom option:

| Size | vCPU | Memory | Disk |
| - | - | - | - |
| **Small** | 1 | 1 GiB | 10 GiB |
| **Medium** | 2 | 4 GiB | 20 GiB |
| **Large** | 4 | 8 GiB | 50 GiB |
| **Custom** | Your value | Your value, in GiB | Your value, in GiB |

Pick **Small** for shell work and short scripts, **Medium** for test suites and dependency installs, **Large** for builds and anything that keeps several processes hot.

## Per-organization ceilings

**Custom** is bounded. Your organization has one ceiling per box:

| Resource | Ceiling per box |
| - | - |
| Compute | 4 vCPU |
| Memory | 32 GiB |
| Storage | 120 GiB |

The console shows these under **Box limits** on the Billing page, with the reason:

> Limits mitigate misuse and keep box and compute capacity fairly available across all users.

Read your current ceilings in [Managing billing](/cloud/billing#per-box-resource-ceilings). Split a workload that wants more than one box can hold across several boxes rather than trying to raise a single box past the ceiling.

## The SDK's sizing fields

`BoxOptions` accepts `cpus`, `memory_mib`, and `disk_size_gb`. Their types, units, and general behavior live in [Compute resources](/manage-sandbox/compute-resources) — the console sizes above are the verified way to size a Cloud box, so set the size in the console when you want a specific shape.

The disk field is named `disk_size_gb`. `disk_gib` is a common guess and fails at construction with a no-such-field error.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| - | - | - |
| `BoxOptions(disk_gib=20)` fails with a no-such-field error | The field is `disk_size_gb` | Use `BoxOptions(disk_size_gb=20)`. See [Compute resources](/manage-sandbox/compute-resources) |
| A box request asks for more CPU, memory, or disk than your organization allows | Ceilings are 4 vCPU compute, 32 GiB memory, and 120 GiB storage per box | Lower the request, or spread the work across several boxes. Check your ceilings in [Managing billing](/cloud/billing#per-box-resource-ceilings) |

## Next steps

> [card] [Boxes](/cloud/boxes)
>
> Everything else about configuring a box on Cloud.


# Boxes
Source: https://docs.boxlite.ai/cloud/boxes

A box on BoxLite Cloud is a microVM you address by name or id from anywhere your API key reaches — choose its image and size, and know when the platform stops it.

A box on BoxLite Cloud is a microVM you address by name or id from anywhere your API key reaches. You choose its image and its size when you create it, and the platform decides when it stops and whether it wakes again.

> [!WARNING]
