# Checkpoints: save and reuse a box
Source: https://docs.boxlite.ai/cloud/checkpoints

Prepare a workspace once, save a checkpoint, and create independent boxes from it with Python, TypeScript, or CLI.

Set up your tools and project once. Save a **checkpoint**, then create independent boxes with the same files and configuration.

A checkpoint captures a stopped box's disk and execution configuration. It does not preserve memory or running processes, and each restored box gets a new ID.

## Create a checkpoint and restore two boxes

Create a project file, save it in a checkpoint, and restore it in a new box. Then change one copy and create another: the second starts from your saved baseline.

```mermaid theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
flowchart LR
    S[Prepared workspace] --> C[Stop and save checkpoint]
    C --> A[Worker 1: change to branch-a]
    C --> B[Worker 2: original baseline]
```

### Before you start

Use a [Cloud API key](/cloud/api-keys) with permission to create and delete boxes. This walkthrough creates one source box, two workers, and one checkpoint.

**CLI:** follow the steps below in the same terminal. **Python or TypeScript:** install your SDK below, then run the [complete example](#complete-sdk-examples). The SDK snippets in each step explain the corresponding part of that program.

> [tab] CLI
>
> Install the latest CLI and log in, pasting your Cloud API key at the prompt:
>
> ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> curl -fsSL https://sh.boxlite.ai | sh
> boxlite --context app auth login --url https://api.boxlite.ai --method api-key
> ```
>
> `app` names your saved context. Keep this Bash or Zsh terminal open for every step below.

> [tab] Python
>
> ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> python3 -m venv .venv
> source .venv/bin/activate
> python -m pip install --upgrade boxlite
> ```
>
> The complete example prompts for your Cloud API key.

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> Install the SDK and enter your Cloud API key on your workstation (Bash or Zsh):
>
> ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> npm install @boxlite-ai/boxlite tsx
> read -r -s BOXLITE_API_KEY
> export BOXLITE_API_KEY
> ```

### 1. Prepare your workspace

Create a box and write a project file containing `baseline`. In your own workflow, this is where you would install tools or prepare project files before saving them.

> [tab] CLI
>
> ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> SOURCE=$(boxlite --context app create --auto-stop 0 --auto-delete 0 python:alpine)
> printf 'Source: %s\n' "$SOURCE"
> boxlite --context app start "$SOURCE" >/dev/null
> boxlite --context app exec "$SOURCE" -- sh -c "mkdir -p /workspace; printf 'baseline\n' > /workspace/project.txt; sync"
> boxlite --context app exec "$SOURCE" -- cat /workspace/project.txt
> ```

> [tab] Python
>
> ```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> source = await runtime.create(boxlite.BoxOptions(
>     image="python:alpine", auto_stop=0, auto_delete=0,
> ))
> print("Source:", source.id)
> await source.start()
> await run(source, "mkdir -p /workspace; printf 'baseline\n' > /workspace/project.txt; sync")
> await run(source, "cat /workspace/project.txt")
> ```

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> ```typescript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> var source = await runtime.create({ image: 'python:alpine', autoStop: 0, autoDelete: 0 });
> console.log('Source:', source.id);
> await source.start();
> await run(source, "mkdir -p /workspace; printf 'baseline\n' > /workspace/project.txt; sync");
> await run(source, 'cat /workspace/project.txt');
> ```

The final line should be:

```text theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
baseline
```

Save the printed source ID. The example disables idle-stop and automatic deletion so the box stays available while you work. Clean up at the end; choose your production [lifecycle settings](/cloud/box-lifecycle) before capturing your own box.

### 2. Save a checkpoint

Stop the source before capture, then wait for the checkpoint to become `ready`. Keep the source stopped until capture finishes.

> [tab] CLI
>
> ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> boxlite --context app stop "$SOURCE"
> boxlite --context app inspect "$SOURCE" --format '{{.State.Status}}'
> ```
>
> Continue only when the status is `stopped`. If needed, repeat the inspect command. Then capture the box:
>
> ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> CHECKPOINT=$(boxlite --context app checkpoint create "$SOURCE")
> printf 'Checkpoint: %s\n' "$CHECKPOINT"
> boxlite --context app checkpoint get "$CHECKPOINT"
> ```
>
> Repeat `boxlite --context app checkpoint get "$CHECKPOINT"` until `state` is `ready`. If it is `failed`, read `error_reason` and stop here.

> [tab] Python
>
> ```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> await source.stop()
> # Wait until the source status is stopped (see complete example).
> checkpoint = await runtime.checkpoints.create(source.id)
> # Wait until checkpoint.state is ready before creating a worker.
> ```

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> ```typescript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> await source.stop();
> // Wait until the source status is stopped (see complete example).
> const checkpoint = await runtime.checkpoints.create(source.id);
> // Wait until checkpoint.state is ready before creating a worker.
> ```

**Do not proceed until the checkpoint is `ready`.** Save its printed ID: you can use it again from another session, even after deleting the source box.

### 3. Restore and verify your files

Create a new box using only the checkpoint. No image or configuration overrides are needed: the saved settings are inherited.

> [tab] CLI
>
> ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> WORKER1=$(boxlite --context app create --checkpoint "$CHECKPOINT")
> printf 'Worker 1: %s\n' "$WORKER1"
> boxlite --context app start "$WORKER1" >/dev/null
> boxlite --context app exec "$WORKER1" -- cat /workspace/project.txt
> ```

> [tab] Python
>
> ```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> worker1 = await runtime.create(boxlite.BoxOptions(checkpoint=checkpoint.id))
> print("Worker 1:", worker1.id)
> await worker1.start()
> await run(worker1, "cat /workspace/project.txt")
> ```

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> ```typescript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> var worker1 = await runtime.create({ checkpoint: checkpoint.id });
> console.log('Worker 1:', worker1.id);
> await worker1.start();
> await run(worker1, 'cat /workspace/project.txt');
> ```

The new box prints `baseline` even though you never wrote that file into it. Its worker ID is different from the source ID.

### 4. Create an independent second copy

Change the first worker's file to `branch-a`, then create a second worker from the same checkpoint. Read both files:

> [tab] CLI
>
> ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> boxlite --context app exec "$WORKER1" -- sh -c "printf 'branch-a\n' > /workspace/project.txt"
> WORKER2=$(boxlite --context app create --checkpoint "$CHECKPOINT")
> printf 'Worker 2: %s\n' "$WORKER2"
> boxlite --context app start "$WORKER2" >/dev/null
> boxlite --context app exec "$WORKER1" -- cat /workspace/project.txt
> boxlite --context app exec "$WORKER2" -- cat /workspace/project.txt
> ```

> [tab] Python
>
> ```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> await run(worker1, "printf 'branch-a\n' > /workspace/project.txt")
> worker2 = await runtime.create(boxlite.BoxOptions(checkpoint=checkpoint.id))
> print("Worker 2:", worker2.id)
> await worker2.start()
> await run(worker1, "cat /workspace/project.txt")
> await run(worker2, "cat /workspace/project.txt")
> ```

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> ```typescript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> await run(worker1, "printf 'branch-a\n' > /workspace/project.txt");
> var worker2 = await runtime.create({ checkpoint: checkpoint.id });
> console.log('Worker 2:', worker2.id);
> await worker2.start();
> await run(worker1, 'cat /workspace/project.txt');
> await run(worker2, 'cat /workspace/project.txt');
> ```

After the second worker ID, you should see:

```text theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
branch-a
baseline
```

The first worker contains your change. The second starts from the saved baseline: editing a worker does not change the checkpoint or other workers.

**Your checkpoint is still available.** Keep it to create more workers, or remove the demo resources when you are done.

### 5. Clean up when you are done

Keep the checkpoint if you want to create more workers. When finished, remove the demo resources yourself; none of the examples delete them automatically.

For the CLI walkthrough, the IDs are still in your shell variables:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
boxlite --context app rm --force "$WORKER1" "$WORKER2" "$SOURCE"
boxlite --context app checkpoint delete "$CHECKPOINT"
```

For an SDK run, or after closing the terminal, use the printed IDs with the [cleanup commands](#clean-up). The workers remain running until you stop or remove them.

## Complete SDK examples

Run one of these programs after installing its dependencies above. It performs steps 1–4, prints each resource ID, and leaves the checkpoint and boxes available for you to explore. Run step 5 when you are done.

If a run fails, keep the IDs already printed and inspect those resources before retrying.

> [accordion] Python: complete runnable example
>
> Save as `checkpoint_demo.py`:
>
> ```python checkpoint_demo.py theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> import asyncio
> from getpass import getpass
> import boxlite
>
> async def main():
>     runtime = boxlite.Boxlite.rest(boxlite.BoxliteRestOptions(
>         url="https://api.boxlite.ai",
>         credential=boxlite.ApiKeyCredential(getpass("BoxLite Cloud API key: ")),
>     ))
>
>     async def run(box, command):
>         execution = await box.exec("sh", args=["-c", command])
>         async def read(stream):
>             return "".join([chunk async for chunk in stream])
>         output, error = await asyncio.gather(
>             read(execution.stdout()), read(execution.stderr()))
>         result = await execution.wait()
>         if result.exit_code != 0:
>             raise RuntimeError(f"Command failed ({result.exit_code}): {error}")
>         print(output.strip())
>
>     try:
>         source = await runtime.create(boxlite.BoxOptions(
>             image="python:alpine", auto_stop=0, auto_delete=0,
>         ))
>         print("Source:", source.id)
>         await source.start()
>         await run(source, "mkdir -p /workspace; printf 'baseline\n' > /workspace/project.txt; sync")
>         await run(source, "cat /workspace/project.txt")
>
>         await source.stop()
>         for _ in range(60):
>             if (await runtime.get_info(source.id)).state.status == "stopped":
>                 break
>             await asyncio.sleep(1)
>         else:
>             raise TimeoutError(f"Check source status: {source.id}")
>
>         checkpoint = await runtime.checkpoints.create(source.id)
>         print("Checkpoint:", checkpoint.id)
>         for _ in range(180):
>             checkpoint = await runtime.checkpoints.get(checkpoint.id)
>             if checkpoint.state == "ready":
>                 break
>             if checkpoint.state in ("failed", "deleting"):
>                 raise RuntimeError(f"{checkpoint.state}: {checkpoint.error_reason}")
>             await asyncio.sleep(1)
>         else:
>             raise TimeoutError(f"Check checkpoint status: {checkpoint.id}")
>
>         print(checkpoint.state)
>
>         worker1 = await runtime.create(boxlite.BoxOptions(checkpoint=checkpoint.id))
>         print("Worker 1:", worker1.id)
>         await worker1.start()
>         await run(worker1, "cat /workspace/project.txt")
>
>         await run(worker1, "printf 'branch-a\n' > /workspace/project.txt")
>         worker2 = await runtime.create(boxlite.BoxOptions(checkpoint=checkpoint.id))
>         print("Worker 2:", worker2.id)
>         await worker2.start()
>         await run(worker1, "cat /workspace/project.txt")
>         await run(worker2, "cat /workspace/project.txt")
>         print("Keep these IDs to reuse the checkpoint or clean up later.")
>     finally:
>         runtime.close()
>
> asyncio.run(main())
> ```
>
> ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> python checkpoint_demo.py
> ```

> [accordion] TypeScript: complete runnable example
>
> Save as `checkpoint_demo.ts`:
>
> ```typescript checkpoint_demo.ts theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> async function main() {
>   const key = process.env.BOXLITE_API_KEY;
>   if (!key) throw new Error('Set BOXLITE_API_KEY on your workstation');
>   var { ApiKeyCredential, BoxliteRestOptions, JsBoxlite } = await import('@boxlite-ai/boxlite');

>     url: 'https://api.boxlite.ai',
>     credential: new ApiKeyCredential(key),
>   }));

>     const stdout = await execution.stdout();
>     const stderr = await execution.stderr();
>     async function read(stream: typeof stdout) {
>       let text = '';
>       for (let chunk = await stream.next(); chunk !== null; chunk = await stream.next()) text += chunk;
>       return text;
>     }

>     console.log(output.trim());

>       if (['failed', 'deleting'].includes(checkpoint.state)) {
>         throw new Error(`${checkpoint.state}: ${checkpoint.errorReason}`);
>       }
>       await sleep();
>     }
>     if (checkpoint.state !== 'ready') throw new Error(`Check checkpoint status: ${checkpoint.id}`);
>     console.log(checkpoint.state);
>
>     var worker1 = await runtime.create({ checkpoint: checkpoint.id });
>     console.log('Worker 1:', worker1.id);
>     await worker1.start();
>     await run(worker1, 'cat /workspace/project.txt');
>
>     await run(worker1, "printf 'branch-a\n' > /workspace/project.txt");
>     var worker2 = await runtime.create({ checkpoint: checkpoint.id });
>     console.log('Worker 2:', worker2.id);
>     await worker2.start();
>     await run(worker1, 'cat /workspace/project.txt');
>     await run(worker2, 'cat /workspace/project.txt');
>     console.log('Keep these IDs to reuse the checkpoint or clean up later.');
>   } finally {
>     runtime.close();
>   }

> main().catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode = 1; });
> ```

## Capture your own box

Finish writes and stop your application's work before stopping the box. Check that its status is `stopped`; checkpoint creation does not stop it for you. Keep it stopped and available until the checkpoint reaches `ready`.

A source box **cannot have attached volumes or Secrets**. Save reusable tools and project files in a box without those attachments. Files already written into its root disk are included in the checkpoint, so remove credentials you do not want copied before capture.

You can give a checkpoint a memorable name:

> [tab] Python
>
> ```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> checkpoint = await runtime.checkpoints.create(source.id, name="prepared-workspace")
> ```

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> ```typescript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> const checkpoint = await runtime.checkpoints.create(source.id, 'prepared-workspace');
> ```

> [tab] CLI
>
> ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> boxlite --context app checkpoint create '<SOURCE_BOX_ID>' --name prepared-workspace
> boxlite --context app checkpoint get prepared-workspace
> ```

Creation returns before capture finishes. Use the waiting loop from step 2, or query the checkpoint until it is `ready`:

| State | What to do |
| - | - |
| `creating` | Wait and query again; do not delete or restart the source. |
| `ready` | Create boxes from the checkpoint; you can now change or delete the source. |
| `failed` | Read `error_reason`, resolve the cause, and create a new checkpoint. |
| `deleting` | Wait for deletion to finish; do not use it for new boxes. |

Names accept letters, digits, `.`, `_`, and `-`, start with a letter or digit, and have at most 128 characters. Omitting a name generates one. Get, create-from-checkpoint, and delete accept an ID or name.

## Reuse a checkpoint in another session

Use its saved ID or name in `BoxOptions(checkpoint=...)`, `{ checkpoint: ... }`, or `boxlite create --checkpoint ...`. An optional new box name is the only creation override.

Do not also pass an image, resource settings, empty lists, or lifecycle defaults: restored boxes inherit the saved configuration, and overrides are rejected.

## What is preserved?

| Preserved | Behavior after restoration |
| - | - |
| Root disk | Files, installed packages, and project changes exist as they did at capture time. |
| Execution configuration | Environment variables, entrypoint, command, user, and working directory are inherited. |
| Resource and placement settings | CPU, memory, disk, region, and class are inherited; creation still needs quota and available capacity. |
| Network and lifecycle configuration | Saved settings are inherited, including idle-stop and automatic deletion. |

Memory, running processes, and open connections are not preserved. A restored box has a new identity. Reconnect clients to that new box, and launch your application through its saved startup command or a new execution.

Checkpoint restoration creates a new box; it does not roll back or replace an existing box. For ongoing data shared across boxes, use [Volumes](/cloud/volumes). For restarting the same box, see [Box lifecycle](/cloud/box-lifecycle).

## List and inspect checkpoints

> [tab] Python
>
> ```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> items = await runtime.checkpoints.list()
> info = await runtime.checkpoints.get("prepared-workspace")
> print(info.id, info.state, info.size_bytes, info.error_reason)
> ```

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> ```typescript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> const items = await runtime.checkpoints.list();
> const info = await runtime.checkpoints.get('prepared-workspace');
> console.log(info.id, info.state, info.sizeBytes, info.errorReason);
> ```

> [tab] CLI
>
> ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> boxlite --context app checkpoint list
> boxlite --context app checkpoint get prepared-workspace
> ```

SDK and CLI list operations fetch all pages. CLI lists also support `--format json`, `--format yaml`, or `--quiet` for IDs only. Do not combine `--quiet` with `--format`.

## Clean up

A ready checkpoint is independent of its source. Deleting the source does not delete the checkpoint; deleting the checkpoint does not delete boxes already restored from it.

If you have closed the walkthrough session, replace the placeholders with the IDs it printed. Run these commands from a terminal logged into the `app` context:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
boxlite --context app rm --force '<WORKER_1_ID>' '<WORKER_2_ID>' '<SOURCE_BOX_ID>'
boxlite --context app checkpoint delete '<CHECKPOINT_ID>'
```

For checkpoint deletion, `force=True` (Python), `true` (TypeScript), or `--force` (CLI) only ignores a missing checkpoint. It does not bypass an active capture or restore operation.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Next step |
| - | - |
| Source must be idle and stopped | Stop it, wait for `stopped`, and let pending operations finish before capturing. |
| Volumes or secrets are not supported | Use a source without those attachments. |
| Saved settings must be inherited | Remove every creation option except `checkpoint` and the new box name. |
| Waiting times out | Query the existing checkpoint by its printed ID; a client timeout does not establish that the server failed. |
| Creating a worker times out | Inspect the box ID in the error, or look it up by the name you supplied, before creating another. |
| Checkpoint is being created or used | Wait for the operation to finish. If restoration failed, remove the failed target box before retrying deletion. |
| Checkpoint limit reached | List your checkpoints and delete unneeded ones. |

For differences from local snapshots and portable archives, see [Cloud vs open source](/cloud/vs-opensource).


# Stop paying for boxes you have finished with
Source: https://docs.boxlite.ai/cloud/cost-controls

The two lifecycle controls that decide how long each half of a box’s bill runs, and the volume pattern that keeps data without keeping a disk.

Compute billing stops on its own. Disk billing does not. These are the controls that close that second loop.

## Which half of the bill each control closes

Two lifecycle controls decide how long each half of the bill runs, and their defaults
pull in opposite directions:

| Control | Default | What it does to your bill |
| - | - | - |
| `auto_stop` | 900 seconds (15 minutes idle) | **Compute billing stops on its own.** After 15 idle minutes the box stops, and vCPU and memory come off the bill |
| `auto_delete` | `0`, disabled | **Disk billing never stops on its own.** A stopped box keeps its disk, and keeps being charged for it, indefinitely |

So by default you stop paying for compute automatically, and you pay for disk forever. Setting `auto_delete` closes that second loop.

## Cap a box's lifetime

`auto_delete` must be larger than `auto_stop` when both are non-zero. This example gives
a box 15 idle minutes to be reused, then deletes it an hour after it stops:

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
# costCappedBox.py — create a box that cleans itself up
# Run: python costCappedBox.py
import asyncio
import os
import time

from boxlite import ApiKeyCredential, Boxlite, BoxliteRestOptions, BoxOptions

IMAGE = "ghcr.io/boxlite-ai/boxlite-agent-base:v0.1.0"

async def main() -> None:
    api_key = os.environ.get("BOXLITE_API_KEY")
    if not api_key:
        raise SystemExit("Set BOXLITE_API_KEY to your blk_live_... key first.")

    rt = Boxlite.rest(BoxliteRestOptions(
        url=os.environ.get("BOXLITE_REST_URL", "https://api.boxlite.ai"),
        credential=ApiKeyCredential(api_key),
    ))

    box = None
    try:
        box = await rt.create(
            BoxOptions(
                image=IMAGE,
                auto_stop=900,     # stop after 15 idle minutes -> compute billing ends
                auto_delete=3600,  # delete an hour after stopping -> disk billing ends
            ),
            name=f"capped-{int(time.time())}",
        )
        await box.start()
        print(f"box {box.id} will delete itself an hour after it stops")
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"create failed: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
        if box is not None:
            await rt.remove(box.id, force=True)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

```typescript Node.js theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
// costCappedBox.ts — create a box that cleans itself up
// Run: node costCappedBox.ts
import { ApiKeyCredential, BoxliteRestOptions, JsBoxlite } from "@boxlite-ai/boxlite";

const IMAGE = "ghcr.io/boxlite-ai/boxlite-agent-base:v0.1.0";

const apiKey = process.env.BOXLITE_API_KEY;
if (!apiKey) {
  throw new Error("Set BOXLITE_API_KEY to your blk_live_... key first.");
}

async function main(): Promise<void> {
  const rt = JsBoxlite.rest(
    new BoxliteRestOptions({
      url: process.env.BOXLITE_REST_URL ?? "https://api.boxlite.ai",
      credential: new ApiKeyCredential(apiKey),
    }),
  );

  let box = null;
  try {
    box = await rt.create(
      {
        image: IMAGE,
        autoStop: 900, // stop after 15 idle minutes -> compute billing ends
        autoDelete: 3600, // delete an hour after stopping -> disk billing ends
      },
      `capped-${Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000)}`,
    );
    await box.start();
    console.log(`box ${box.id} will delete itself an hour after it stops`);
  } catch (err) {
    console.error(`create failed: ${err}`);
    if (box) {
      await rt.remove(box.id, true);
    }
  }
}

main();
```

```go Go theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
// costCappedBox.go — create a box that cleans itself up
// Run: go run costCappedBox.go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"time"

	boxlite "github.com/boxlite-ai/boxlite/sdks/go"
)

const image = "ghcr.io/boxlite-ai/boxlite-agent-base:v0.1.0"

func main() {
	apiKey := os.Getenv("BOXLITE_API_KEY")
	if apiKey == "" {
		fmt.Println("Set BOXLITE_API_KEY to your blk_live_... key first.")
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	restURL := os.Getenv("BOXLITE_REST_URL")
	if restURL == "" {
		restURL = "https://api.boxlite.ai"
	}

	rt, err := boxlite.NewRest(boxlite.BoxliteRestOptions{
		URL:        restURL,
		Credential: boxlite.NewApiKeyCredential(apiKey),
	})
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("connect failed: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	defer rt.Close()

	ctx := context.Background()
	box, err := rt.Create(ctx, image,
		boxlite.WithName(fmt.Sprintf("capped-%d", time.Now().Unix())),
		boxlite.WithAutoStopInterval(900),    // compute billing ends after 15 idle minutes
		boxlite.WithAutoDeleteInterval(3600), // disk billing ends an hour after stopping
	)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("create failed: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	if err := box.Start(ctx); err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("start failed: %v\n", err)
		_ = rt.Remove(ctx, box.ID())
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	fmt.Printf("box %s will delete itself an hour after it stops\n", box.ID())
}
```

See [Lifecycle on Cloud](/cloud/box-lifecycle) for the full semantics of these fields,
including how `auto_resume` brings a stopped box back.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **From the CLI you can set only half of this.** `boxlite create` accepts `--auto-stop`,
> and takes a friendlier duration than the SDK — `30s`, `15m`, `2h`, `7d` rather than raw
> seconds:
>
> ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> boxlite create python --name worker --auto-stop 15m
> ```
>
> `--auto-delete` is refused on a box made this way, because `boxlite create` makes a
> detached box:
>
> ```
> Error: invalid argument: remove-on-stop is incompatible with detach=true.
> Detached boxes should use auto_delete=0 ... for manual lifecycle control.
> ```
>
> To close the disk half of the bill, set `auto_delete` from an SDK, as above.

## Keep the data, drop the disk

`auto_delete` is uncomfortable when the box holds something you need later. That is what volumes are for, and it happens to be the cheapest arrangement available:

* A **managed volume** is not part of a box's metered resources. Mounting one adds nothing to the box's hourly price.
* A **stopped box** is billed for its disk for as long as it exists.

So when you want to keep results but not keep paying, write them to a volume and let the box go. See [Volumes](/cloud/volumes).

# Keep data when the box is gone
Source: https://docs.boxlite.ai/cloud/data-across-boxes

Write to a volume from one box, delete that box, and read the same data back from a new one — the reason managed volumes exist.

A box’s own disk dies with the box. A volume does not. This walks the proof end to end: write from one box, delete it, then read the same bytes from a box that did not exist when they were written.

## Prerequisites

* An API key from the console, exported as `BOXLITE_API_KEY`. See [API keys](/cloud/api-keys).
* `pip install boxlite`, and the REST URL exported as `BOXLITE_REST_URL`. See [Quickstart](/cloud/quickstart).

Every example reads both values from the environment, so nothing hard-codes a credential.

## See it in six commands

The whole proof, from a terminal. Box A writes, box A is destroyed, box B reads what A
left behind:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
boxlite volume create --name handoff-demo

boxlite create python --name box-a -v handoff-demo:/data && boxlite start box-a
boxlite exec box-a -- sh -c 'echo "produced by box A" > /data/handoff.txt'
boxlite rm -f box-a                      # the box is gone, the volume is not

boxlite create python --name box-b -v handoff-demo:/data && boxlite start box-b
boxlite exec box-b -- cat /data/handoff.txt
# produced by box A
```

`boxlite volume` talks to a REST server, so run `boxlite auth login` first — see
[`boxlite volume`](/reference/cli#boxlite-volume).

## Do the same from code

The property that makes a volume worth using: write through the mount in one box,
destroy that box, mount the same volume in a different box, and the data reads back.
The volume is backed by managed storage, not by the box.

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
import asyncio
import os
import time

from boxlite import (
    ApiKeyCredential,
    Boxlite,
    BoxliteRestOptions,
    BoxOptions,
)

# A name is easier to carry between processes than an id.
VOLUME = os.environ.get("BOXLITE_VOLUME", "<YOUR_VOLUME_NAME>")
IMAGE = "ghcr.io/boxlite-ai/boxlite-agent-base:v0.1.0"

async def run_in_fresh_box(rt, name, script):
    """Create a box with the volume mounted, run one shell script, then remove the box."""
    box = await rt.create(
        BoxOptions(image=IMAGE, volumes=[(VOLUME, "/data")]),
        name=name,
    )
    try:
        await box.start()
        execution = await box.exec("sh", args=["-c", script])
        output = ""
        async for line in execution.stdout():
            output += line
        result = await execution.wait()
        return result.exit_code, output
    finally:
        # The box is gone after this line; the volume is not.
        await rt.remove(box.id, force=True)

async def main():
    rt = Boxlite.rest(BoxliteRestOptions(
        url=os.environ.get("BOXLITE_REST_URL", "https://api.boxlite.ai"),
        credential=ApiKeyCredential(os.environ["BOXLITE_API_KEY"]),
    ))
    stamp = int(time.time())

    try:
        # Box A writes, then is destroyed.
        code, _ = await run_in_fresh_box(
            rt,
            f"volume-writer-{stamp}",
            "echo 'produced by box A' > /data/handoff.txt",
        )
        if code != 0:
            print(f"box A write failed with exit code {code}")
            return

        # Box B is a different box on the same volume.
        code, output = await run_in_fresh_box(
            rt,
            f"volume-reader-{stamp}",
            "cat /data/handoff.txt",
        )
        print(f"box B exit code: {code}")
        print(f"box B read back: {output}")
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"handoff failed: {exc}")

asyncio.run(main())
```

```typescript Node.js theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
import { ApiKeyCredential, BoxliteRestOptions, JsBoxlite } from "@boxlite-ai/boxlite";

// A name is easier to carry between processes than an id.
const VOLUME = process.env.BOXLITE_VOLUME ?? "<YOUR_VOLUME_NAME>";
const IMAGE = "ghcr.io/boxlite-ai/boxlite-agent-base:v0.1.0";

// Create a box with the volume mounted, run one shell script, then remove the box.
async function runInFreshBox(rt, name: string, script: string): Promise<[number, string]> {
  const box = await rt.create({ image: IMAGE, volumes: [[VOLUME, "/data"]] }, name);
  try {
    await box.start();
    const execution = await box.exec("sh", ["-c", script]);
    const stdout = await execution.stdout();
    let output = "";
    while (true) {
      const line = await stdout.next();
      if (line === null) break;
      output += line;
    }
    const result = await execution.wait();
    return [result.exitCode, output];
  } finally {
    // The box is gone after this line; the volume is not.
    await rt.remove(box.id, true);
  }
}

async function main(): Promise<void> {
  const rt = JsBoxlite.rest(
    new BoxliteRestOptions({
      url: process.env.BOXLITE_REST_URL ?? "https://api.boxlite.ai",
      credential: new ApiKeyCredential(process.env.BOXLITE_API_KEY!),
    }),
  );
  const stamp = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);

  try {
    // Box A writes, then is destroyed.
    const [writeCode] = await runInFreshBox(
      rt,
      `volume-writer-${stamp}`,
      "echo 'produced by box A' > /data/handoff.txt",
    );
    if (writeCode !== 0) {
      console.error(`box A write failed with exit code ${writeCode}`);
      return;
    }

    // Box B is a different box on the same volume.
    const [readCode, output] = await runInFreshBox(rt, `volume-reader-${stamp}`, "cat /data/handoff.txt");
    console.log(`box B exit code: ${readCode}`);
    console.log(`box B read back: ${output}`);
  } catch (err) {
    console.error(`handoff failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : err}`);
  } finally {
    rt.close();
  }
}

main();
```

```bash REST theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
# Two boxes, one volume: the first writes, the second reads after the first is gone.
BOXLITE_REST_URL="${BOXLITE_REST_URL:-https://api.boxlite.ai}"
VOLUME="${BOXLITE_VOLUME:-<YOUR_VOLUME_NAME>}"
IMAGE="ghcr.io/boxlite-ai/boxlite-agent-base:v0.1.0"
AUTH=(-H "Authorization: Bearer ${BOXLITE_API_KEY}" -H 'Content-Type: application/json')

make_box() {
  curl -fsS -X POST "${BOXLITE_REST_URL}/v1/boxes" "${AUTH[@]}" \
    -d "{\"image\":\"${IMAGE}\",\"volumes\":[{\"managed_volume\":\"${VOLUME}\",\"guest_path\":\"/data\"}]}" \
    | jq -r .id
}

# Box A writes, then is destroyed.
A=$(make_box)
curl -fsS -X POST "${BOXLITE_REST_URL}/v1/boxes/${A}/exec" "${AUTH[@]}" \
  -d '{"command":"sh","args":["-c","echo '"'"'produced by box A'"'"' > /data/handoff.txt"]}' > /dev/null
# exec is asynchronous: it returns an execution id. Wait for it before
# removing the box, or the write can still be in flight.
EXEC_ID=$(curl -fsS -X POST "${BOXLITE_REST_URL}/v1/boxes/${A}/exec" "${AUTH[@]}" \
  -d '{"command":"sh","args":["-c","true"]}' | jq -r .id)
for _ in $(seq 30); do
  STATE=$(curl -fsS "${BOXLITE_REST_URL}/v1/boxes/${A}/executions/${EXEC_ID}" "${AUTH[@]}" | jq -r .state)
  [ "$STATE" = "completed" ] && break
  sleep 1
done

curl -fsS -X DELETE "${BOXLITE_REST_URL}/v1/boxes/${A}?force=true" "${AUTH[@]}"

# Box B is a different box on the same volume.
B=$(make_box)
curl -fsS -X POST "${BOXLITE_REST_URL}/v1/boxes/${B}/exec" "${AUTH[@]}" \
  -d '{"command":"cat","args":["/data/handoff.txt"]}'
curl -fsS -X DELETE "${BOXLITE_REST_URL}/v1/boxes/${B}?force=true" "${AUTH[@]}"
```

## Only what is under the mount path survives

This is the part people get wrong. The volume is mounted at one path, and **only what
you write under that path** outlives the box:

| Where box A writes | After box A is destroyed |
| - | - |
| `/data/handoff.txt` — under the mount | Still there, readable from box B |
| `/root/notes.txt` — the box's own disk | Gone |
| `/tmp/anything` | Gone |

If something you expected to survive did not, check which side of the mount path it was
written to before suspecting the volume.

> [card] [Volumes](/cloud/volumes)
>
> What a volume is, the full parameter reference, and how Cloud differs from open source.


# Give your service a fixed public domain
Source: https://docs.boxlite.ai/cloud/domains

Reach a service inside a Cloud box through a named HTTPS address, and keep that address when you move to another box.

Give a web app, API, or agent service a public address such as `https://my-service.boxliteapp.com`. Visitors use that address while BoxLite routes requests to a port inside your box.

The domain belongs to your organization. You can move it to another box without changing the address your clients use.

> [!NOTE]
>
> This guide uses a subdomain you choose under BoxLite's domain. Attaching a domain you own, such as `api.your-company.com`, is not supported by this flow. No DNS records or TLS certificates need to be configured for the BoxLite-provided address.

## Before you start

Install the latest CLI in your local terminal:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
curl -fsSL https://sh.boxlite.ai | sh
```

Create an [API key](/cloud/api-keys) in the [console](https://app.boxlite.ai), then sign in:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
boxlite --context app auth login \
  --url https://api.boxlite.ai --method api-key
```

Paste your key at the prompt. `app` is the saved context used throughout this guide. Use the same organization in the console and CLI.

## Publish your service

**1. Reserve your domain**

In the console, open **Domains**, then **Request domain**. Enter a short name, such as `my-service`, and review the **Full domain** preview before submitting.

Choose an available name using lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens. The page shows your organization's name-length requirement and remaining allowance.

Copy the full hostname into your terminal, replacing the placeholder below. Include neither `https://` nor a port:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
DOMAIN='<YOUR_FULL_DOMAIN>'
```

For example, if you reserved `my-service`, the production hostname is `my-service.boxliteapp.com`. Use the hostname actually returned by your environment.

Already have a domain? Reuse it instead of requesting another:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
boxlite --context app domain ls
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> Reserving a name uses your organization's domain allowance. Unbinding it later keeps the name reserved and does not free that allowance.

**2. Choose the service to expose**

> [tab] Existing service
>
> Set the box ID or name and the port your service listens on **inside the box**:
>
> ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> BOX='<YOUR_BOX_ID_OR_NAME>'
> PORT=29090
> boxlite --context app start "$BOX"
> ```
>
> Replace `29090` with your service's port. The service must listen on `0.0.0.0`, rather than only `127.0.0.1`.

> [tab] Try a sample server
>
> Create a box with an HTTP server as its saved startup command:
>
> ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> BOX=$(boxlite --context app create \
>   --name domain-demo \
>   --auto-stop 0 --auto-delete 0 \
>   python:alpine python -m http.server 29090 --bind 0.0.0.0)
> PORT=29090
> boxlite --context app start "$BOX"
> ```
>
> The sample serves a directory listing. `--auto-stop 0` keeps it running until you stop it; request-triggered startup is optional.

**3. Open the port and bind the domain**

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
boxlite --context app network inbound "$BOX" enabled
boxlite --context app network tunnel "$BOX" "$PORT"
boxlite --context app domain bind "$DOMAIN" \
  --type box --box "$BOX" --port "$PORT"
```

The tunnel command registers the port for public access and prints its generated URL. The bind command gives that port your chosen hostname and prints its HTTPS URL.

All three pieces are required: inbound access, a public tunnel for the port, and the domain binding. Binding alone does not make a service public.

This is a public endpoint. If your service needs sign-in or API authentication, enforce it in the application.

**4. Open your fixed URL**

Open `https://<YOUR_FULL_DOMAIN>` in your browser, or request it from your terminal:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
curl --fail --show-error \
  -H 'X-BoxLite-Skip-Preview-Warning: true' \
  "https://$DOMAIN/"
```

The header skips the preview notice for scripted requests; it does not grant access or bypass your application's authentication.

You should receive your service's response. For the sample server, look for **Directory listing for /**. Share this HTTPS address with your clients; they do not need the box ID or internal port.

## Move the service without changing its URL

Start your service on the replacement box first. Then open its port and bind the **same domain** to it:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
NEW_BOX='<YOUR_REPLACEMENT_BOX_ID_OR_NAME>'
NEW_PORT=29090
boxlite --context app start "$NEW_BOX"
boxlite --context app network inbound "$NEW_BOX" enabled
boxlite --context app network tunnel "$NEW_BOX" "$NEW_PORT"
boxlite --context app domain bind "$DOMAIN" \
  --type box --box "$NEW_BOX" --port "$NEW_PORT"
```

New requests to the fixed URL now reach the replacement service. You do not need to unbind first or reserve another name.

This changes routing; it does not copy files or application state. Prepare any data the new service needs before switching. See [Data across boxes](/cloud/data-across-boxes).

## Optional: wake the box on a request

You can keep the service running continuously, or let the box stop between requests. The fixed domain works with either approach.

For request-triggered startup, leave **Wake on access** enabled and save your service as the box's startup command. The sample above already does this. A server started only in an interactive session may not return after a restart.

To try it, stop the box, wait until the console shows **Stopped**, and request the same URL:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
boxlite --context app stop "$BOX"
# Wait for Stopped in the console before sending this request.
curl --fail --show-error \
  -H 'X-BoxLite-Skip-Preview-Warning: true' \
  "https://$DOMAIN/"
```

The request starts the box and reaches the service. Allow extra time for startup on the first request.

For automatic idle stopping, choose a nonzero `--auto-stop` interval when creating the box. See [Stop when idle](/cloud/box-lifecycle#stop-when-idle) and [Wake on access](/cloud/box-lifecycle#wake-on-access).

## Unbind or close public access

To stop routing the domain while keeping it for later:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
boxlite --context app domain unbind "$DOMAIN"
boxlite --context app domain ls
```

New requests to the domain return `404`. The name remains reserved, and the list shows no target.

**Unbinding leaves the generated tunnel URL accessible.** To close public access to that port as well:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
boxlite --context app network tunnel --revoke "$BOX" "$PORT"
```

If you created the sample box and no longer need it, delete it:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
boxlite --context app rm --force "$BOX"
```

Deleting a box does not release its domain or automatically clear its binding. Unbind or point the domain at another box explicitly.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | What to check |
| - | - |
| The CLI does not recognize `domain` | Install the latest CLI and check `boxlite domain --help`. |
| `domain_not_owned` when binding | Reserve the name first, use its full hostname, and select the same organization and environment in the CLI. |
| The domain allowance is full | Reuse a held domain from `domain ls`; unbinding does not free a slot. |
| The domain returns `404` | Check its binding, inbound access, and the port's public tunnel. Private or revoked tunnels do not serve named domains. |
| The request fails even though the binding exists | Confirm the service is running on the bound port and listening on `0.0.0.0`. |
| A stopped box does not serve the next request | Check Wake on access and the saved service startup command. |
| The domain reaches the wrong service | Inspect `domain ls` and bind it to the intended box and port. |


# Pin a build, and roll it back
Source: https://docs.boxlite.ai/cloud/image-aliases

Give the build you tested a name production can boot, move that name on release, and move it back when a release goes wrong.

A tag moves whenever someone pushes. An **alias** does not: it is a name you attach to one exact build in [your catalog](/cloud/image-catalog), and it only moves when you move it.

Point `stable` at the build you tested, create boxes from `stable`, and when the next release is ready, move the alias. When that release is wrong, move it back. Nothing touches the registry.

## Pin the build you tested

> [tab] Console
>
> Open **Images**, choose the image, and pin a name to the version you want from its row.

> [tab] SDK
>
> An alias points at a build, identified by its digest, so read the build first:
>
> ```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> detail = await rt.images.get("ghcr.io/acme/api")
> digest = detail.versions[0].digest
>
> await rt.images.create_alias(
>     name="ghcr.io/acme/api",
>     alias="stable",
>     digest=digest,
> )
> ```
>
> `alias` must be valid tag syntax; `digest` must be `sha256:` and 64 hex digits. Anything else is refused before it reaches the catalog.

## Boot it

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
box = await rt.create(
    BoxOptions(image="ghcr.io/acme/api:stable"),
    name="prod-worker",
)
```

## Promoting and rolling back are one operation

There is no separate move call. Point the same alias at a different build and it is there instead:

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
# Promote: stable now means the build you just tested
await rt.images.create_alias(
    name="ghcr.io/acme/api", alias="stable", digest=new_digest,
)

# Roll back: stable means the previous one again
await rt.images.create_alias(
    name="ghcr.io/acme/api", alias="stable", digest=previous_digest,
)
```

Boxes created afterwards boot the build the alias now names. **Boxes already running are untouched** — a rollback does not restart anything, so recycle them yourself if that is what you need.

## Finding the build to roll back to

The catalog keeps every move, naming the build on each side of it. That history is how you find what `stable` meant before:

> [tab] Console
>
> The image's page shows each version and the names currently on it.

> [tab] SDK
>
> ```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> detail = await rt.images.get("ghcr.io/acme/api")
> for event in detail.history:
>     print(event.alias, event.from_digest, "->", event.to_digest, event.recorded_at)
> ```
>
> `from_digest` is empty the first time an alias is created.

## Remove an alias

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
await rt.images.delete_alias(name="ghcr.io/acme/api", alias="stable")
```

The build stays in the catalog; only the name you gave it is gone.

## Things that will bite you

* **An alias is not a tag.** A tag is part of the reference the image was pulled as, and the catalog records it read-only. An alias is yours, and is the only part you can move.
* **An alias belongs to one image name.** `stable` on `ghcr.io/acme/api` has nothing to do with `stable` on another repository.
* **The CLI cannot do this.** Aliases are a console or SDK operation.

## Next

> [card] [The catalog](/cloud/image-catalog)
>
> Where builds and their history are kept, and the limit they count against.

> [card] [Private images](/cloud/private-images)
>
> Pinning works the same on images from a private registry.


# What the catalog records
Source: https://docs.boxlite.ai/cloud/image-catalog

Every image your boxes have booted is recorded once, outlives the box, and counts against a limit — here is how to see it and clear it.

The first time a box boots an image, that image is recorded in your organization's **catalog**. The catalog is what makes [aliases](/cloud/image-aliases) possible, and it is what the image limit counts.

## Seeing it

> [tab] Console
>
> The **Images** page lists every recorded image with its tags, size, how many boxes use it, and when it last started. The header shows where you stand against the limit:
>
> ```text theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> 1 of 20 images · 3.5 MiB
> ```
>
> Built-in images appear in their own row at the bottom, marked **free · not counted**.

> [tab] SDK
>
> ```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> images = await rt.images.list()        # one entry per reference
> usage  = await rt.images.usage()       # count, limit, bytes
> detail = await rt.images.get("docker.io/library/alpine")
> ```
>
> `usage()` answers with the three numbers behind the console's header:
>
> ```text theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> ImageUsage(count=1, limit=20, known_bytes=3630321)
> ```
>
> `list()` gives one entry per reference — enough to know what you have used. `get()` opens one name up into every build the catalog has seen of it, which aliases point where, and how those aliases have moved. Versions and history live only on `get()`.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **`boxlite images` does not read this catalog.** It lists the images on the machine you run it from, whether or not `BOXLITE_REST_URL` is set.

## Two things about the timing

**Recording happens when the box boots, not when `create()` returns.** In a measured run the entry appeared about **12 seconds** later. Code that creates a box and immediately reads the catalog usually finds nothing, so poll:

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
for _ in range(10):
    if await rt.images.list():
        break
    await asyncio.sleep(4)
```

A box removed before it boots leaves nothing recorded at all.

**The record outlives the box.** Removing a box does not remove its image. That is normally what you want — the next box from the same image starts without re-pulling — but it is also why a catalog fills up with nothing running.

## The limit

Each organization's catalog holds **20** images.

**Built-in images do not count.** `base`, `python`, `node`, and the others BoxLite maintains are free and sit outside the limit, so a catalog can read `0 of 20` while boxes run on them continuously.

Aliases do not count either. Ten aliases on one image are still one image.

Once the limit is reached, creating a box from an image not already recorded fails. The create is refused; no box is left behind.

## Clearing space

`last_used_at` on each version is the signal — a build nothing has booted in weeks is the safe one to drop.

> [tab] Console
>
> Find the image on the **Images** page. The **BOXES** column shows whether anything still uses it; remove it from the row's action menu.

> [tab] SDK
>
> ```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> detail = await rt.images.get("docker.io/library/alpine")
> for v in detail.versions:
>     print(v.digest[:19], v.last_used_at, v.size_bytes)
>
> await rt.images.remove("docker.io/library/alpine")
> ```

Removing an image takes its versions, aliases, and history with it. An image a running box still uses cannot be removed.

## Next

> [card] [Pin a build](/cloud/image-aliases)
>
> Name a build so you know which one to keep and which to clear.

> [card] [What a box costs](/cloud/box-costs)
>
> Images are not metered. Boxes and their disks are.


# Images
Source: https://docs.boxlite.ai/cloud/images

The images BoxLite maintains for you, and how to start a box from one of your own instead.

Every box starts from an image. BoxLite maintains four of them, ready to use with no setup:

| Image | What it is |
| - | - |
| `base` | A general-purpose Linux box you install into yourself |
| `python` | Python, ready to run |
| `node` | Node.js, ready to run |
| `sandbaseai-hermes` | The Hermes agent, preinstalled |

They are free and do not count against your image limit.

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
box = await rt.create(BoxOptions(image="python"), name="demo")
```

## Or bring your own

Name any image on a public registry and a box boots it — nothing to upload, build, or approve first:

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
box = await rt.create(BoxOptions(image="ghcr.io/acme/api:1.4.0"), name="demo")
```

> Start a box from any public registry, and see what gets recorded. **Start here.**

> [card] [Pin a build](/cloud/image-aliases)
>
> Make production boot the exact build you tested, and move it back when a release goes wrong.

> [card] [Private images](/cloud/private-images)
>
> Register a registry login once, then reference private images like any other.

>
> What is recorded when a box boots, and the limit it counts against.

## Where to do what

| | Console | SDK | CLI |
| - | - | - | - |
| Start a box from any image | Yes | Yes | `boxlite run <image>` |
| See which images you have used | **Images** page | `rt.images.list()` | No |
| Pin a build, roll one back | **Images** page | `rt.images.create_alias()` | No |
| Register a private registry login | **Private registries** tab | `rt.images.registries` | No |

> [!WARNING]
>
> **`boxlite images` does not show the Cloud catalog.** It lists images on the machine you run it from, with or without `BOXLITE_REST_URL` set. Use the console or `rt.images.list()`.

Reach for the console to do something once. Reach for the SDK when it has to happen without you.


# BoxLite Cloud
Source: https://docs.boxlite.ai/cloud/index

The managed cloud for AI agents — compute, a filesystem that outlives the box, a public URL, and hardware isolation around all of it, from a URL and an API key.

**The managed cloud for AI agents.** Your agent gets compute, a filesystem that survives a restart, a public URL for whatever it builds, and hardware-level isolation around all of it — from a URL and an API key.

You run no hosts, cache no images, and plan no capacity. A box starts in about a second, stops itself when it goes idle, and wakes when something reaches for it again.

Cloud is not a separate client library. It is the same `boxlite` package you install locally, and the runtime handle is the only line that changes:

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
import os

from boxlite import ApiKeyCredential, Boxlite, BoxliteRestOptions

# The one line that differs from running BoxLite on your own machine.
rt = Boxlite.rest(
    BoxliteRestOptions(
        url=os.environ["BOXLITE_REST_URL"],  # https://api.boxlite.ai
        credential=ApiKeyCredential(os.environ["BOXLITE_API_KEY"]),
    )
)
```

Everything after that line — `create`, `exec`, volumes, tunnels — is the API you already know. The [Quickstart](/cloud/quickstart) has the whole first script, end to end.

## Start here

> [card] [Quickstart](/cloud/quickstart)
>
> Create a key, install the SDK, run your first command on Cloud.

> [card] [Hand it to a coding agent](https://boxlite.ai/agent.md)
>
> `agent.md` is a single file written for coding agents. Every code block in it is executed against the live API before release.

> [card] [Cloud vs open source](/cloud/vs-opensource)
>
> Every difference between the hosted runtime and self-hosted BoxLite, in one table — plus how to port existing code.

## Two shapes, one API

The same `rt.create()` call gives you either shape. What differs is how long the box lives.

> [card] A disposable box
>
> Run untrusted or model-generated code, take the result, throw the box away. Hardware-level isolation without a virtualization host of your own.

> [card] A home for an agent
>
> One box that keeps its filesystem, its packages, and its working state across sessions. The agent installs its tools once instead of rebuilding its world on every run.

The second shape is what a stateful microVM makes possible, and it is the part a plain sandbox API cannot do: an agent writes files, stops, and picks the work back up a week later.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Idle means no SDK, terminal, or preview traffic.** Work running *inside* the box does not count, so a long unattended job can be stopped mid-run. Set the idle window per box — see [Stop when idle](/cloud/box-lifecycle#stop-when-idle).

## What you get

> [card] [Boxes](/cloud/boxes)
>
> Shared Linux base images, three preset sizes, and a managed lifecycle. Up to **4 vCPU, 32 GiB memory, and 120 GiB storage** per box.

> [card] [Volumes](/cloud/volumes)
>
> Managed storage that outlives the box that wrote it. Mount by a name you choose, and volumes are not metered at all.

> [card] [Network](/cloud/network)
>
> A tunnel to a port inside the box, carrying a public URL — so what your agent builds is reachable without you deploying it.

> [card] [Checkpoints](/cloud/checkpoints)
>
> Save a prepared box and create independent workers from its disk and configuration.

> [card] [Secrets](/cloud/secrets)
>
> Let a box authenticate to external APIs without storing real keys in its environment.

> [card] [Domains](/cloud/domains)
>
> Give a service a fixed public HTTPS address, and keep it when you move to another box.

> [card] [Pricing](/cloud/pricing)
>
> Three metered rates and nothing else. Run wallet-only with no subscription, or take a plan whose quota covers usage first.

Concurrency is set by your plan — 20 boxes on Starter, 100 on Pro, 1000 on Max. See [Wallet or a plan?](/cloud/plans) for which one your usage argues for.

## Build something

Six things people ship on Cloud, each a complete runnable guide:

> [card] [Run Claude Code in a box](/agent-in-box/run-claude-code)
>
> An autonomous coding agent with root inside its own kernel and nothing outside the box.

> [card] [Code interpreter for an LLM](/use-cases/code-interpreter)
>
> A model writes Python, it executes in a disposable box, the box is thrown away.

> [card] [Review untrusted pull requests](/use-cases/sandboxed-ci)
>
> Clone the PR into a box, run the suite, read the diff — with no access to your machine.

> [card] [Data analysis agent](/use-cases/data-analysis-agent)
>
> CSV in, model-written pandas analysis and a chart out.

> [card] [Scrape the web safely](/use-cases/web-scraping-agent)
>
> A browser box feeding clean data to a model, with parsing in a separate box.

> [card] [A persistent shell per user](/use-cases/interactive-dev-environment)
>
> State survives stop and restart, so every user or branch keeps its own environment.


# Create a volume and mount it into a box
Source: https://docs.boxlite.ai/cloud/mount-a-volume

Create a managed volume, mount it into a box at a path you choose, and write and read through the mount.

A managed volume is storage the platform keeps for you, independent of any box. This is
the shortest complete path: create one, mount it, write through it, read it back.

## Pick where to do this

Creating a volume takes one step on any of three surfaces. Mounting one always happens
where the box is created, so that part follows whichever you use to make boxes.

> [tab] Console
>
> 1. Open **Volumes** and click **New Volume**.
> 2. Fill in **Name** — the only field. Pick something you will recognize later, such as
>    `subtitle-models`.
> 3. Creation waits until the volume is ready, so you can mount it immediately.
>
> Use the console when you want to **see what you own**. `rt.volumes.list()` and the
> **Volumes** page report the same set, and a name set in either place mounts the same way.

> [tab] CLI
>
> ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> boxlite volume create --name subtitle-models   # prints the volume id
> boxlite create python --name trainer -v subtitle-models:/data
> boxlite start trainer
> boxlite exec trainer -- sh -c 'echo hi > /data/f.txt && cat /data/f.txt'
> ```
>
> `boxlite volume` talks to a REST server, so run `boxlite auth login` first. Flag tables
> are on the [CLI reference](/reference/cli#boxlite-volume).

> [tab] SDK
>
> The script below is the whole flow — create, mount, write, read. Use this when the
> volume is part of something your program does rather than something you set up once.

## Prerequisites

* An API key from the console, exported as `BOXLITE_API_KEY`. See [API keys](/cloud/api-keys).
* `pip install boxlite`, and the REST URL exported as `BOXLITE_REST_URL`. See [Quickstart](/cloud/quickstart).

Every example reads both values from the environment, so nothing hard-codes a credential.

Create a volume, mount it into a box at `/data`, write a file through the mount, and read it back. This runs as written once the two environment variables are set.

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
# cloud_volume.py — create a named volume, mount it, write and read through it
# Run: python cloud_volume.py
import asyncio
import os
import time

from boxlite import (
    ApiKeyCredential,
    Boxlite,
    BoxOptions,
    BoxliteRestOptions,
)

IMAGE = "ghcr.io/boxlite-ai/boxlite-agent-base:v0.1.0"

api_key = os.environ.get("BOXLITE_API_KEY")
if not api_key:
    raise SystemExit("Set BOXLITE_API_KEY to your blk_live_... key before running this.")


async def main() -> None:
    rt = Boxlite.rest(
        BoxliteRestOptions(
            url=os.environ.get("BOXLITE_REST_URL", "https://api.boxlite.ai"),
            credential=ApiKeyCredential(api_key),
        )
    )

    volume = None
    box = None
    try:
        # rt.volumes is a property. create() takes an optional name that you can
        # mount by later, instead of carrying the id around.
        volume = await rt.volumes.create(f"demo-{int(time.time())}")
        print(f"Created volume {volume.name} (id {volume.id})")

        box = await rt.create(
            BoxOptions(
                image=IMAGE,
                # (managed volume name or id, mount path inside the box)
                volumes=[(volume.name, "/data")],
            ),
            name=f"volume-demo-{int(time.time())}",
        )
        await box.start()

        # Write through the mount, not to the box's own disk.
        write = await box.exec(
            "sh",
            args=["-c", "echo 'subtitle model v3' > /data/notes.txt"],
        )
        write_result = await write.wait()
        if write_result.exit_code != 0:
            print(f"write failed with exit code {write_result.exit_code}")
            return

        read = await box.exec("cat", args=["/data/notes.txt"])
        content = ""
        async for line in read.stdout():
            content += line
        read_result = await read.wait()

        print(f"Exit code: {read_result.exit_code}")
        print(content)
    except Exception as exc:
        # Auth failures, creation failures, and local runtimes without a volume
        # backend all surface here.
        print(f"volume run failed: {exc!r}")
    finally:
        # Teardown in finally, so a failure above cannot leave a box billing.
        if box is not None:
            await rt.remove(box.id, force=True)
        if volume is not None:
            await rt.volumes.remove(volume.id)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

```typescript Node.js theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
// cloudVolume.ts — create a named volume, mount it, write and read through it
// Run: node cloudVolume.ts
import { ApiKeyCredential, BoxliteRestOptions, JsBoxlite } from "@boxlite-ai/boxlite";

const IMAGE = "ghcr.io/boxlite-ai/boxlite-agent-base:v0.1.0";

const apiKey = process.env.BOXLITE_API_KEY;
if (!apiKey) {
  throw new Error("Set BOXLITE_API_KEY to your blk_live_... key before running this.");
}

async function main(): Promise<void> {
  const rt = JsBoxlite.rest(
    new BoxliteRestOptions({
      url: process.env.BOXLITE_REST_URL ?? "https://api.boxlite.ai",
      credential: new ApiKeyCredential(apiKey),
    }),
  );

  const stamp = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
  let volume = null;
  let box = null;
  try {
    // rt.volumes is a property. create() takes an optional name you can mount by.
    volume = await rt.volumes.create(`demo-${stamp}`);
    console.log(`Created volume ${volume.name} (id ${volume.id})`);

    box = await rt.create(
      {
        image: IMAGE,
        // [managed volume name or id, mount path inside the box]
        volumes: [[volume.name, "/data"]],
      },
      `volume-demo-${stamp}`,
    );
    await box.start();

    // Write through the mount, not to the box's own disk.
    const write = await (await box.exec("sh", ["-c", "echo 'subtitle model v3' > /data/notes.txt"])).wait();
    if (write.exitCode !== 0) {
      console.error(`write failed with exit code ${write.exitCode}`);
      return;
    }

    const read = await box.exec("cat", ["/data/notes.txt"]);
    const stdout = await read.stdout();
    let content = "";
    while (true) {
      const line = await stdout.next();
      if (line === null) break;
      content += line;
    }
    const result = await read.wait();

    console.log(`Exit code: ${result.exitCode}`);
    console.log(content);
  } catch (err) {
    // Auth failures, creation failures, and local runtimes without a volume
    // backend all surface here.
    console.error(`volume run failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : err}`);
  } finally {
    // Teardown in finally, so a failure above cannot leave a box billing.
    if (box !== null) await rt.remove(box.id, true);
    if (volume !== null) await rt.volumes.remove(volume.id);
    rt.close();
  }
}

main();
```

```bash REST theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
# Requires BOXLITE_API_KEY. Create a key in the console: /cloud/api-keys
BOXLITE_REST_URL="${BOXLITE_REST_URL:-https://api.boxlite.ai}"
IMAGE="ghcr.io/boxlite-ai/boxlite-agent-base:v0.1.0"
NAME="demo-$(date +%s)"

# 1. Create a named volume. An empty body creates an unnamed one, whose name
#    the server sets to the id.
VOLUME=$(curl -fsS -X POST "${BOXLITE_REST_URL}/v1/volumes" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${BOXLITE_API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"name\":\"${NAME}\"}")
echo "${VOLUME}" | jq '{id, name, state}'

# 2. Mount it by name. The wire field is managed_volume — it takes a name or an id.
curl -fsS -X POST "${BOXLITE_REST_URL}/v1/boxes" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${BOXLITE_API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"image\":\"${IMAGE}\",\"volumes\":[{\"managed_volume\":\"${NAME}\",\"guest_path\":\"/data\"}]}" \
  | jq '{id, name}'

# 3. Clean up when you are done.
curl -fsS -X DELETE "${BOXLITE_REST_URL}/v1/volumes/$(echo "${VOLUME}" | jq -r .id)" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${BOXLITE_API_KEY}"
```

Two things in that script are worth pausing on, and the rest of this page builds on them: the volume carries a **name you chose**, and the box mounts it by that name.

# Network
Source: https://docs.boxlite.ai/cloud/network

Reach a service running inside a Cloud box, and control what that box is allowed to reach on the way out.

A box that runs a web app, a dev server, or an SSH daemon is only useful once something can reach it. On BoxLite Cloud you ask a box for a **tunnel** to one of its ports, and that tunnel gives you a public URL and a byte stream. What the box itself may reach on the way out is a separate control.

Two rules hold across everything here:

* **Your service must bind `0.0.0.0`.** A tunnel arrives on the box's network interface, so a server on `127.0.0.1` inside the box is unreachable.
* **A tunnel carries exactly one connection.** Ask for a fresh one per request, per retry, and per concurrent client.

## In this section

> [card] [How tunnels work](/cloud/tunnels)
>
> The concept, the one-shot rule, what a tunnel is verified to carry, and the full parameter reference. **Start here.**

> [card] [Serve HTTP](/cloud/serve-http)
>
> Start an HTTP server inside a box, get its public URL, and make a request over it.

> [card] [Port forwarding](/cloud/port-forwarding)
>
> Publish a box port on your own machine so `curl`, a browser, or a database driver can dial it.

> [card] [Raw streams](/cloud/raw-streams)
>
> Take the byte stream directly when you are speaking a protocol of your own.

> [card] [Network policy](/cloud/network-policy)
>
> Who can reach a box — public, private, signed URLs — and the egress allowlist that bounds what it reaches.

## Which page do I want?

| You want | Page |
| - | - |
| To understand the model before writing code | [How tunnels work](/cloud/tunnels) |
| A fixed public hostname that can move between boxes | [Domains](/cloud/domains) |
| A public URL for an HTTP service in a box | [Serve HTTP](/cloud/serve-http) |
